plugins.readme_text:
# Agent Team Console

Read-only Agent Teams dashboard for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI (`dsh-agent-team-console`): a
project-scoped, visual-first live stage for every team, with workspace-first headers, animated agent
nodes, and rounds / token / working-time statistics in one first-class main panel.

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Repository: <https://github.com/kkomia/dsh-agent-team-console>

> **Unofficial community plugin.** This repository is not part of the DeepSeek official packages, is
> not published or endorsed by DeepSeek, and is not a replacement for the official experimental
> Agent Teams bundle. It is a read-only viewer: it never creates, changes, or completes a team
> member or a task.

## Why this plugin

The official experimental Agent Teams Web UI (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-client-ui-agent-team`)
adds a compact roster and task-board action to the conversation header. That is convenient for a
quick check while you are inside the Lead conversation, but it is not a page of its own.

Agent Team Console keeps the same read-only contract and adds a sidebar entry plus a full main
panel for people who keep a team running for a long stretch:

- A project filter and a compact status strip covering in-progress tasks, running members, token
  usage, blocked tasks, and pending tasks.
- Workspace-first team headers with a working-vs-idle donut plus team rounds and token totals.
- An animated SVG agent stage: one node per member, sized by token usage and ringed by working time.
- A one-line task summary with in-progress rows on demand, so the page stays visual instead of a wall
  of text.

It is a plain DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web plugin: no build step for users, no npm dependencies, and no
external services.

## Features

- **Sidebar entry and main panel.** A sidebar item labelled "Team console" (the Chinese UI shows
  "团队看板") opens a dedicated page in the main area.
- **Project filter.** When more than one project (workspace) has live teams, a select appears in the
  header. It defaults to "All projects" and narrows the status strip and the team list to one project;
  the choice is client-side and is not persisted.
- **In-progress-first status strip.** A single compact row of five chips: in-progress tasks, running
  members (running / total), token usage for the current selection, blocked tasks (pending tasks that
  are not ready), and pending tasks. Zero values stay visible but muted.
- **Workspace-first team sections.** Teams are ordered active first, then by most recent activity.
  Each team header starts with the prominent workspace/project name (falling back to "No project",
  "未分组" in the Chinese UI), then the Lead name and role, a status dot, a working-vs-idle donut with
  a "work · idle" caption, team rounds, team token totals, an in-progress count when non-zero, and the
  expand/collapse toggle. Active teams expand by default; idle teams stay collapsed.
- **Animated agent stage.** The text roster is replaced by an SVG stage with one node per member (Lead
  first and slightly larger; up to 8 shown, then a "+N" overflow node). Node radius scales with token
  usage, an outer arc shows the working ratio, and the status ring animates: running pulses and
  orbits, provisioning spins a dashed ring, idle is muted and static, and failed is a static error
  ring. Under each node sits a tiny "N rounds · X tok" line.
- **Member details on hover or focus.** Hovering or focusing a node opens a compact detail card with
  the model, rounds, steps, token breakdown (uncached input, cache read, cache write, output, total),
  and working and idle time. Clicking the node opens the member's session when workspace navigation is
  available.
- **Compact task summary.** Each team shows one line with in-progress, pending, and blocked counts and
  a small expand toggle. Expanding shows only the in-progress tasks as one-line rows (subject, owner);
  pending and completed tasks stay counts only. Blocked follows the readiness rule: only a pending
  task with `ready === false` is blocked, and in-progress tasks are never shown as blocked.
- **Activity stays in the API.** The snapshot still carries the bounded activity list for API
  consumers, but the v1.2 panel no longer renders it.
- **Multiple teams and projects.** One collapsible section per live team, filtered by project when a
  project is selected.
- **Honest states.** A loading skeleton on first load, an error card with retry, a "showing the last
  successful snapshot" hint after a failed poll, an unsupported-service notice, and an empty state.
- **Bilingual.** All visible copy goes through the DSH client locale service, with Chinese and
  English dictionaries kept in sync; the panel follows the host language.
- **Theme-native.** Colors, borders, and SVG art come only from `--dsw-*` theme tokens, so the panel
  follows dark and light themes. Stage nodes are keyboard accessible and every animation is disabled
  under reduced motion.
- **Polling.** The panel refreshes a same-origin JSON snapshot every 2 seconds while it is mounted and
  the tab is visible, pauses while the tab is hidden, and offers a manual refresh button.
- **Optional navigation.** When the host exposes `uiWorkspace.openSession`, clicking a stage node
  opens that member's session. When it does not, the panel stays a read-only page.

## Requirements and compatibility

- **DSH Web UI** in the desktop app or a Web profile. The plugin was developed and tested against DSH
  `0.2.1-rc.2`; `package.json` declares `engines.dsh` as `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`, which also excludes
  0.3.0 prereleases.
- **The official experimental Agent Teams bundle must be mounted in the same profile.** This plugin
  visualizes teams that already exist; it does not provide the Agent Teams service itself. Without
  that service the panel shows a clear "not mounted" notice instead of failing.
- **Optional session projections.** Rounds, token usage, and working / idle times come from the stock
  DSH `sessionStats` and `tokenUsage` projections. They are optional: without them the panel still
  renders the stage and shows dashes for statistics.
- **A Web-capable profile.** The install examples below use the `desktop` profile; replace `desktop`
  with your own Web profile name (`web`, and so on) if it differs.
- **No separate Node.js installation is needed to use the plugin.** Node.js 22.19 or newer is only
  needed to run the tests in this repository.

## Install

The examples below use `dsh plugin --profile desktop add <spec>`. Replace `desktop` with your profile
name if you use a different Web profile.

### From the app Plugins page

1. Open **Plugins** in the DSH desktop app.
2. Choose **Add plugin**.
3. Paste `github:kkomia/dsh-agent-team-console` (or `dsh-agent-team-console` once the package is
   published on npm), then confirm the install.
4. Restart the app so the host half loads, then open the Web UI.

### From the command line

GitHub repository (works today):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:kkomia/dsh-agent-team-console
```

npm registry (once the package is published on npm):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-agent-team-console
```

GitHub installs are resolved through the network and need Git (and pnpm, which DSH's plugin manager
already uses). The repository has no build step, so the install is a plain copy of the package files.

### Activation

The host half registers an HTTP route when the DSH host process starts, so **restart the desktop app
after installing or upgrading**; then refresh the Web UI page if it is already open. If only client
assets changed and the host is unchanged, a page refresh is enough.

## Usage

### Open the panel

Select **Team console** in the sidebar. The panel loads the current snapshot immediately and then
keeps polling every 2 seconds while it is visible.

### Read the header

The header shows the page title and subtitle (a one-line description of the live stage), the project
filter when it applies, a live indicator (pulsing while any member is running), the time of the last
successful update, and a refresh button that spins while a manual refresh is in flight.

plugins.description: Native Rapid-MLX provider for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) — dsh reads model facts from the server instead of your settings.yaml.
plugins.readme_text:
# @raullenchai/dsh-provider

A native [Rapid-MLX](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX) provider for
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — so `dsh`
gets its model facts from the server instead of from whatever you typed into
`settings.yaml`.

[![CI](https://github.com/raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

> **Status: published to npm** as
> [`@raullenchai/dsh-provider`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@raullenchai/dsh-provider).
> The end-to-end `dsh` run in [Verified](#verified) was on an M3 Ultra against
> `dsh 0.1.0-rc.7`; `dsh 0.1.0-rc.8` is API-compatible — the `LlmAdapter`
> contract is byte-identical and the only changes are additive — and the
> adapter is re-verified against rc.8 at the protocol and unit-test level.
> DSH is still a developer preview that moves fast, so treat this as tracking
> a moving target, not a frozen compatibility promise.

## What it does for you

DSH can already talk to a local Rapid-MLX server through its generic
`openai-completions` provider. That route works — but it knows nothing about
your model beyond what you hand-wrote:

```yaml
# what the generic route makes you maintain, by hand, per model
llm-pi-ai:
  providers:
    rapid-mlx:
      baseURL: http://localhost:8000/v1
      defaultContextWindow: 262144      # you looked this up. is it still right?
      models:
        - id: qwen3.6-35b-8bit
          contextWindow: 262144
          reasoningEfforts: {off: none, low: low, medium: medium, high: high}
```

Rapid-MLX's `/v1/models` already publishes all of that and more. This adapter
reads it, so:

**1. Nothing to hand-write, and nothing to re-write when you switch models.**
Swap what `rapid-mlx serve` is running and `dsh` follows. No re-running setup,
no stale numbers.

**2. The reasoning control tells the truth.** Rapid-MLX reports whether a model
actually has a reasoning parser. A model that can't reason no longer shows an
off/low/medium/high selector that does nothing.

**3. Compaction is timed with the capacity that actually fits this Mac, not a
number that drifted.** This is the one that quietly costs you.
`dsh-compaction-basic` asks the provider for the route's capacity and compacts
at `thresholdRatio × capacity` (0.8 by default). The provider prefers the
server's **`max_model_len`** — Rapid-MLX's memory-fitted ceiling (what fits in
unified memory: weights + KV cache), in the vLLM/SGLang-standard field — over
the native `context_window`, and falls back to `context_window` on an older
server that doesn't report it. So compaction is timed to what the machine can
actually hold, not the model's advertised window (which it may not have room
for) and not a hand-written number copied from another model.

## Install

Needs Node ≥ 22.15 (dsh imports Node's Zstd stream API without declaring it)
and a running Rapid-MLX server.

```sh
# From npm:
dsh plugin --profile web add @raullenchai/dsh-provider

# …or straight from source — the package ships plain JS with no build step:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:raullenchai/rapid-mlx-dsh-provider

export RAPID_MLX_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1     # optional; this is the default
dsh web
```

Then point the agent at the route:

```yaml
# $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml
agent-default-model:
  provider: rapid-mlx
  model: qwen3.6-35b-8bit
```

Verified: that command installs and activates as a profile layer against
`dsh 0.1.0-rc.7`. To hack on it locally instead, see
[Local development](#local-development).

## Model management (v0.2.0)

Beyond the provider route, the plugin registers five tools and a `/rapid-mlx`
command so the agent can see and manage models without leaving the session.
The split follows which surface actually owns each fact: served-model facts
come from the structured HTTP `/v1/models`; the download cache and pull/remove
are CLI-only, so those — and only those — shell out to `rapid-mlx` through the
harness subprocess seam.

| Tool | Source | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `rapid_mlx_serving` | HTTP `/v1/models` | The model(s) served right now, deduped, with context window, reasoning/tool parsers, MoE/hybrid, and modalities. |
| `rapid_mlx_cached` | `rapid-mlx models --cached` | Downloaded models and their on-disk size. |
| `rapid_mlx_pull` | `rapid-mlx pull <name>` | Download a model (alias or HF repo id). Cancellable; no fixed deadline. |
| `rapid_mlx_remove` | `rapid-mlx rm -y <name>` | Delete a cached model to free disk. |
| `rapid_mlx_health` | HTTP + `rapid-mlx --version` | API up? CLI reachable? Reported as two independent facts. |

`/rapid-mlx` prints a one-shot overview: health, the served model and its facts,
and total cache disk usage.

The CLI is resolved from the `cliCommand` config (default `rapid-mlx` on
`PATH`, or `$RAPID_MLX_CLI`); set it to an absolute path if the binary is not on
the harness's `PATH`. `rapid_mlx_pull`/`rapid_mlx_remove` are the only tools
that change anything on disk, and they run non-interactively (`rm` is forced
with `-y` because the subprocess seam ignores stdin).

## Verified

Against `dsh 0.1.0-rc.7` on an M3 Ultra:

- Installs and **activates as a profile layer** (no "declares no `dsh.bundle`"
  warning; the entry shows up in `dsh --profile headless --dump-config`).
- Registers the `rapid-mlx` route with `ctx.llm` and serves real queries.
- Plain chat, a single tool call, and the multi-step bug-fix task that gates
  Rapid-MLX releases — the last one fixed the bug and made the target repo's own
  test pass, verified independently, in 36 s on `qwen3.6-35b-8bit`.

## Not done yet

Being explicit, because the point of the adapter is to *use* what the server
says and some of it is still only read:

- `recommended_sampling` — should be applied automatically per model.
- `tool_call_parser` — should let `dsh` fail fast on a model that cannot emit
  `tool_calls`, instead of looping.
- `is_hybrid` / `is_moe` / `capabilities` — read, not yet acted on.
- **Memory-aware capacity.** Today `resolveModel()` reports the model's
  *advertised* context window. On a Mac the real ceiling is unified memory, and
  reporting that instead is the biggest remaining win — it needs Rapid-MLX to
  expose a usable-capacity figure first.
- Images are not carried through `stream()` — but they now **refuse** with
  `LlmError(..., 'UNSUPPORTED')` rather than being dropped, per the cookbook.
  Text, reasoning and tool calls are carried.
- The route is registered as `rapid-mlx`. If your `settings.yaml` also declares
  a `rapid-mlx` provider under `llm-pi-ai`, the two compete for one route name
  (`registerAdapter` owns provider exclusivity). Use one or rename ours.

## Conformance with the official adapter contract

Built against
[`docs/cookbook/adding-an-llm-adapter.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/main/docs/cookbook/adding-an-llm-adapter.md)
and its "protocol obligations" section. Each item has a test:

| Obligation | How it is met |
|---|---|
| `usage` before `finish`, nothing after `finish` | usage is buffered and flushed at end-of-stream, so a trailing usage-only chunk cannot reorder it |
| Tool-call `arguments` are raw JSON strings end to end | fragments stream as `argumentsDelta` and reassemble unparsed |
| Block indexes in first-seen order, reused per block | verified across a reasoning-then-text response |
| Errors take exactly two sanctioned paths | transport/protocol failures **throw** `LlmError` with a stable code; nothing ends the stream quietly |
| Honor `options.signal` | passed to `fetch` and to the SSE reader; an `AbortError` is re-thrown unchanged, not reclassified |
| A field the provider cannot honor throws `UNSUPPORTED` | image content refuses instead of being narrowed away |
| Config is a schemastery schema with env fallback | `export const Config`, fed from `cordis.patch.yml` via `!!js process.env.RAPID_MLX_BASE_URL` |

`finish.replayState` is not emitted: Rapid-MLX needs no native response ids
or signatures on follow-up calls, so there is nothing lossless to project.

## Three things worth knowing before you edit this

Each of these cost real

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness 会话自动命名插件：类别 emoji + 对象｜目标
plugins.readme_text:
# 会话标题命名 · Title Oil

为 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 自动整理会话名称，采用 [oil-codex-title](https://github.com/oil-oil/oil-codex-title) 的 **「类别 emoji + 对象｜目标」** 风格，方便在侧边栏区分正在做的事情。

**版本 0.5.0** · **MIT** · 已在 **macOS / DSH Desktop 0.2.0-rc.2** 验证。

这是独立插件，可以单独安装；[会话花费与余额](https://github.com/ygnstudio/dsh-plugin-session-cost) 是另一个可选插件。

## 命名效果

以下为格式示例，实际结果由所选模型生成：

| 会话内容 | 示例标题 |
| --- | --- |
| 排查支付回调重复发货 | 🧩 支付回调｜重复发货修复 |
| 为图像模型评测策划视频 | 🎬 图像模型评测｜视频策划 |
| 调整登录表单的布局 | 🎨 登录表单｜布局优化 |
| 比较数据库方案 | 🔎 数据库｜方案比较 |

- **持续更新**：每条用户消息后，宿主在后台重新评估标题，不打断正文回复。
- **参考实际工作**：读取最近的用户消息，以及上一轮 assistant 回复摘要与工具名称。
- **保持稳定**：当前标题仍准确时保持原样；默认跳过「嗯、好、继续」等纯确认消息。
- **手动命名优先**：在 DSH 中手动改名后，由宿主固定标题，自动命名不再覆盖。
- **规则可配置**：模型、参考消息数、中英文长度和类别都可在应用内调整，保存后生效。

## 安装

### 桌面版：从插件管理器安装（推荐）

1. 打开 DSH 左侧的 **插件 → 添加插件**。
2. 在安装目标中粘贴：

   ```text
   github:ygnstudio/dsh-plugin-title-oil#v0.5.0
   ```

3. 点击安装，完成后选择 **立即启用**。
4. 若管理器提示需要重启，完全退出并重新打开 DSH。打开 **插件 → 会话标题命名** 检查设置页。

源码已是可运行的 JavaScript，**没有构建步骤或安装脚本**。当前通过 GitHub 分发，尚未发布到 npm；无需手写 profile 配置。

DSH 同时只能使用一个自动标题提供者。此插件的 bundle 会关闭内置的 `session-title-llm` 并注册自身；已有其他自动命名插件时，请先在管理器中停用冲突项。

### 使用 `dsh web` 的用户

只对独立的 `web` profile 使用以下命令；桌面版优先使用插件管理器：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:ygnstudio/dsh-plugin-title-oil#v0.5.0
```

安装后重启已有的 `dsh web` 进程并刷新页面。不同 profile 独立安装；这里的 CLI 语法已对照官方实现，Web 版没有完成与桌面版同等的运行验证。

### 从本地源码安装

```sh
git clone --branch v0.5.0 https://github.com/ygnstudio/dsh-plugin-title-oil.git
cd dsh-plugin-title-oil
pwd
```

将 `pwd` 输出的绝对目录填入 **插件 → 添加插件**。宿主提供 DSH 依赖，不需要另外构建。保留该目录，因为本地目录安装可能链接到源码。

## 开始使用

1. 打开 **插件 → 会话标题命名**，或 **设置 → 标题命名**。
2. 选择用于命名的供应商和模型。默认路由为 `deepseek-account / deepseek-flash`；如果当前宿主没有此模型，从下拉列表改选可用模型，或选择「跟随会话路由」。
3. 调整标题规则与分类，点击 **保存修改**。
4. 新建会话并发送有明确内容的消息，观察侧边栏标题更新。
5. 想保留某个标题时，直接在 DSH 中手动重命名会话。

**自动命名会产生独立的模型调用。** 收费、套餐额度与共享规则由所选供应商决定；跟随会话路由也不代表免计费。命名上下文会发送给所选供应商，包含最近消息、assistant 摘要及工具名称。费用插件的主会话估算不包含这类辅助调用。

## 设置项

| 设置 | 默认值 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 命名供应商 / 模型 | `deepseek-account / deepseek-flash` | 可选择已配置路由，或两项一起留空以跟随会话 |
| 参考消息 | 5 条 | 最近的用户消息数，范围 1–20 |
| 中文长度 | 6 字 | 「对象」「目标」每段的期望上限，范围 1–30 |
| 英文长度 | 4 词 | 每段的期望词数，范围 1–20 |
| 跳过纯确认消息 | 开启 | 「嗯、好、继续」等不触发改名 |
| 分类规则 | 5 类 | emoji、名称与描述；删除所有行并保存后恢复内置类别 |
| 输入上限（高级） | 8192 字节 | UTF-8 上下文预算，范围 1024–65536 |
| 输出上限（高级） | 64 tokens | 命名模型最大输出，范围 1–256 |
| 超时（高级） | 30 秒 | 范围 1–120 秒；长输入会优先保留最新意图 |

长度是提示词目标，模型不保证逐字满足。内置类别为 🎬 内容制作、🧩 工具开发、🔎 对比调研、🎨 页面设计、📝 方法整理。

保存失败时保留草稿；并发冲突时可使用「重新载入并替换草稿」读取最新设置。**恢复默认**会清除用户覆盖，回到 bundle 的默认配置，不需要重启。

## 数据与兼容范围

配置默认保存在 `~/.dsh/plugin-data/title-oil/config.overrides.json`。设置了 `DSH_HOME` 时使用其下的 `plugin-data/title-oil/`。目录 0700、配置 0600，采用原子写入。

首次加载会复制旧源码目录中的覆盖配置并保留原件。配置不包含独立保存的模型 API key；模型调用使用 DSH 中已有的供应商配置。

当前验证基线是 macOS / DSH Desktop 0.2.0-rc.2。其他操作系统、宿主版本及模型服务尚未全面验证。插件只有 Web/桌面设置界面，不承诺 TUI 可用。

## 更新与卸载

- **更新**：备份上述数据目录，按插件管理器提示更换到新版本 tag；若要求先卸载再安装，配置目录会保留。
- **停用或卸载**：在插件管理器关闭开关或选择卸载。移除本 bundle 后，内置标题提供者应随其覆盖层解除而恢复；若还有其他配置覆盖，检查标题提供者启用状态。
- **Web CLI**：`dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-plugin-title-oil`，然后重启对应进程。
- 卸载不会删除用户配置，也不会批量改动已有会话标题。

## 常见问题

| 现象 | 处理 |
| --- | --- |
| 标题没变化 | 检查是否手动命名、最新消息是否为纯确认；确认插件启用及命名模型可用 |
| 模型下拉加载失败 | 先确认 DSH 中相同供应商能正常使用；保存的模型会保留，可稍后重试 |
| 提示标题提供者冲突 | 停用其他命名插件，确认只保留一个提供者 |
| 标题更新慢 | 选择响应更快的模型，减少参考消息数或输入预算；模型服务的网络延迟仍有影响 |
| 浏览器直接打开兼容设置 URL 返回 401 | API 使用 DSH 的认证上下文，请从应用内打开设置 |
| 保存提示冲突 | 记录需要保留的修改，重新载入最新配置后再次保存 |

## 开发与验证

开发测试使用 Node.js 22，无需额外安装依赖即可运行策略测试：

```sh
npm test
node --check index.js
node --check client.js
npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts
```

测试覆盖语义目标反转、长中文和 emoji 的 UTF-8 预算，不产生模型调用。Host 运行需要由 DSH 提供 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` 和 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-title`；普通 Node 导入不能代替宿主验证。

已检查真实 DSH 加载、设置页和保存行为；发布检查没有触发付费命名调用，因此不声称覆盖所有模型的实际命名质量。更多细节见 [实现与接口](docs/architecture.md)。

## 许可与致谢

[MIT](LICENSE)。命名规则参考并改编自 [oil-codex-title](https://github.com/oil-oil/oil-codex-title)，运行能力由 DeepSeek Harness 提供。版权与许可保留在 [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。本项目并非 DeepSeek 或 oil-codex-title 的官方插件。

# opencode2dsh **Free OpenCode Zen models, natively inside DSH (DeepSeek Harness).** No API key. No registration. No extra process. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@opencode2dsh%2Fdsh-plugin)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@opencode2dsh%2Fdsh-plugin)](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh/blob/master/LICENSE) [![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A520-brightgreen)](https://nodejs.org) [![DeepSeek Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-plugin-blue)](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh) English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)
--- opencode2dsh registers a native DSH `LlmAdapter` that streams directly from [OpenCode Zen](https://opencode.ai/zen)'s **anonymous free lane** — the same models OpenCode's own CLI uses without an account, served to your DSH model picker as a regular provider called `opencode2dsh`. Requests leave your machine looking exactly like traffic from the OpenCode CLI (same user agent, same correlation headers), and the model catalog stays fresh through a three-tier fallback chain. There is nothing to log into and nothing to host. ## Highlights - **Zero credential, zero setup** — the anonymous lane needs no key; install, restart, chat - **Native adapter, no sidecar** — one npm package, no child process, no binary, no local port (the legacy Go sidecar is not part of the published package; see `legacy/`) - **CLI-identical disguise** — requests carry the OpenCode CLI user agent and its session/request/project header set, derived per conversation - **Selectable thinking levels** — reasoning-capable free models expose an effort picker in DSH's model selector (declared ladders where the model metadata provides them, Off/Minimal/Low/Medium/High otherwise); Responses-only `muse-spark-*` models expose only upstream-supported effort levels, and no selection keeps the provider default - **Image input where it is declared** — image attachments are accepted for every model whose [models.dev](https://models.dev) entry lists `image` in `modalities.input`, and refused for the ones that declare `text` only; models.dev being silent falls back to the live-verified vision family - **Live catalog with a fallback chain** — live upstream list ∩ free-by-metadata, falling back to offline cache and a verified static list - **Self-healing** — fast startup retries, periodic refresh, and a written health snapshot for diagnostics - **Proper error surfaces** — upstream failures (rate limit, auth, timeout, transport) arrive in DSH as classified finish reasons, and retries stay owned by DSH ## Install **From the plugin market** (recommended, once this repo is listed there): in DSH open **Settings → Plugin Market**, search `opencode2dsh`, one-click install. **From npm**: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin ``` **From source** (build the tarball yourself): ```sh git clone https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh.git cd opencode2dsh/packages/plugin pnpm install && pnpm pack dsh plugin --profile web add ./opencode2dsh-dsh-plugin-.tgz ``` **Verify**: restart `dsh web`, open the model picker, and pick a model from the **opencode2dsh** group. Requires DSH (DeepSeek Harness) 0.1.7 or newer with a web profile (the IP 池 settings page rides the 0.1.7 Plugins page contract); Node.js ≥ 20 (already present if DSH runs); outbound HTTPS to `opencode.ai` and `models.dev`. ## Configuration Defaults work out of the box. Override via the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: opencode2dsh name: '@opencode2dsh/dsh-plugin' config: mode: adapter # adapter (default) | sidecar providerId: opencode2dsh refreshSeconds: 300 # catalog refresh cadence ``` | Option | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `mode` | `adapter` | `adapter`: native LlmAdapter streaming straight from Zen. `sidecar`: legacy local-agent mode, not bundled — build the agent from `legacy/agent` and pass `agentPath`. | | `providerId` | `opencode2dsh` | Provider name shown in DSH. | | `refreshSeconds` | `300` | Live catalog refresh interval. Pricing metadata refreshes every 24 h. | | `agentPath` | auto-resolved | Sidecar only: path to the agent binary. | | `agentArgs` | — | Sidecar only: extra CLI args for the agent. | | `restartDelayMs` / `restartMaxDelayMs` / `maxConsecutiveCrashes` | `1000` / `60000` / `5` | Sidecar only: restart backoff and circuit breaker. | | `firstEventMs` / `bodyIdleMs` / `responsesBodyIdleMs` | `30000` / `120000` / `300000` | Adapter only, plugin 0.3.7+: stream-liveness watchdogs, in ms (integers from `1` to `600000`). Time to the first stream event, mid-response body silence, and the body-idle floor for Responses models (`muse-spark-*`). Increase `firstEventMs` for slow cold starts. Unset keeps the defaults; restart DSH after editing. | ## How it works ``` DSH session │ harness chunks (block-start / text-delta / usage / finish …) ▼ ZenAdapter (registered LlmAdapter) │ pi-ai openai-completions stream (chat models) │ pi-ai openai-responses stream (`muse-spark-*`, Responses-only on Zen) ▼ https://opencode.ai/zen/v1 ← Authorization: Bearer public with CLI-identical headers: user-agent: opencode/… x-opencode-client, x-opencode-session, x-session-affinity, X-Session-Id, x-opencode-request, x-opencode-project ``` - **Session correlation** — session/project ids are SHA-256 derived from the conversation's first user turn (stable per conversation, non-reversible), and each request gets a fresh random id, mirroring the CLI. - **Catalog fallback chain** — S1: live `GET /v1/models`; S2: models.dev pricing metadata decides "free"; S3: a compile-time verified static list. A disk cache (~7-day TTL) covers upstream outages. - **Resilience** — the adapter registers immediately at startup; if the first catalog fetch races your network (VPN/TUN reconnects, DNS), the plugin retries on a short cadence (~1 min) before settling into the periodic refresh. - **Sidecar mode** (`mode: sidecar`, legacy) — spawns a local Go agent (a single-tenant port of [opencode2api](https://github.com/jasonxu114514/opencode2api)) on `127.0.0.1:`, token-authenticated, and registers a standard `llm-pi-ai` route. **Not part of the published package**; build it from `legacy/agent` (`go build ./cmd/agent`) and point `agentPath` at the binary. ## Health & troubleshooting The plugin writes a health snapshot after every refresh round: ``` ~/.opencode2dsh/adapter-status.json ``` ```json { "status": "ready", "total": 64, "exposed": 9, "lastError": "", "writtenAt": "2026-08-29T07:01:54.915Z" } ``` | Symptom | Likely cause & fix | | --- | --- | | `403 FreeTierError` / "OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode" | The upstream restricts free-tier clients. The plugin preserves the explanation instead of reporting an invalid API key. Use the supported OpenCode client or an official API service. | | Boot screen shows `Failed to load plugins … list slot "plugins.item" requires options.id`, or the IP 池 entry has no configuration page | Your DSH predates the 0.1.7 Plugins page contract. Upgrade DSH to 0.1.7 (latest recommended). On 0.1.6 and older the page never mounts (it is gated on `configForms.whileServed`) — model routing is unaffected. | | DSH 0.1.7/0.2 cannot start after plugin installation (`pending … settingsScope`) | Upgrade the plugin to 0.3.5. On DSH 0.2, configure IP pooling through the installed opencode2dsh row on the Plugins page. | | Only 3 models | Startup fetch raced your network; retries land within ~1 min. Check `adapter-status.json` for `lastError`. | | `lastError: "fetch failed"` persisting | Outbound HTTPS to `opencode.ai` blocked; check proxy/VPN rules. | | Rate-limit errors in chat (`429 … Endpoint is unavailable`) | The anonymous lane is quota-per-IP and free models are contended. Since the fix for [#51](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh/issues/51) the plugin's provider retry policy rides out 429 bursts silently (8 retries, ~1s→20s backoff, ≈90s worst case per step) instead of sur

# reviso-dsh

Reviso for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) — the DSH surface of the Reviso family.

| repo | surface |
|---|---|
| `reviso` | product (backend + web) |
| `reviso-agent` | agent skill (any agent, platform-agnostic) |
| `reviso-cli` | CLI |
| **`reviso-dsh`** | DSH host integration (this repo) |

## Status: Phase 1 — visible client face (verified in a live browser)

Implemented, two views:
- Sidebar entry (`sidebar.footer.action`, beside Settings) + `shell.overlay` panel — ALL Reviso documents for the user.
- Session view tab (`conversation.view`, id `reviso-dsh.view`, beside chat | trajectory) — documents produced by THIS session (binding key `session_key = dsh:<sessionId>`, served once the reviso L0 contract lands).
Demo mode (labeled 演示) is the default; fill Server + Token in the panel's
连接设置 to hit a real deployment (auth: `Authorization: Bearer <automation
key or account-agent token>`; the deployment must allow this origin via
`REVISO_CORS_ALLOWLIST`).

Slot/build contract: see docs/client-face-contract.md.

Minimal DSH bundle that loads under the harness. Roadmap:

1. **Phase 0 (here)** — bundle skeleton, load-verified locally.
2. **Phase 1** — Reviso HTTP client: publish/read with `source_kind` +
   `source_session_id` (normalized to `session_key`); requires the L0 contract
   in the `reviso` main repo (`document_sources` sidecar + read APIs).
3. **Phase 2** — Agent Inbox tab + per-session "back to session" openers
   (client-face spike against DSH's browser extension contract).

## Concepts (per DSH docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md)

- A **bundle** is an npm package shipping a config layer: `package.json`
  declares `dsh.bundle` → its `cordis.patch.yml` inserts plugin rows that
  reference the package **by name**.
- A **profile** is what a user boots (`dsh --profile <name>`); `dsh plugin`
  maintains it. Layer order: profile bundles → profile patch → home patch →
  `--patch` overlays.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add /path/to/reviso-dsh
dsh --profile <name> --dump-config   # expect a "# == dsh-reviso" layer
```

## Local dev

Scratch form uses an absolute source path (paths must be absolute):

```yaml
# dev.patch.yml
- insert:
    - id: reviso-dsh
      name: '/absolute/path/to/reviso-dsh/index.js'
```

```sh
pnpm dsh web --patch ./dev.patch.yml
```

## Contract

The cross-repo contract (Reviso HTTP API + `source_kind` enum
`dsh|claude|codex|cursor|mcp` + `session_key = kind:normalized_id`) is owned by
the `reviso` main repo (L0). This package never talks to Supabase directly.

Tested with dsh `0.1.0-rc.8`.

## See it locally

`sh
pnpm install && pnpm run build:client   # produce lib/client.js
dsh plugin --profile web add /Users/touchskyer/Code/reviso-projects/reviso-dsh
dsh web                                  # Reviso entry sits beside Settings in the sidebar
`

Rollback: `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-reviso`.

## License

MIT — same as `reviso-agent` / `reviso-cli`.

# dsh-model-picker · 模型速选器（DeepSeek Harness 插件）

[简体中文](README.md) | [English](README.en.md)

在 DeepSeek Harness 会话窗口右下角 **模型下拉框的左侧** 添加一个小按钮。
点击按钮弹出全量模型选择窗口：按提供商分组、实时搜索、提供商筛选、
真实能力标签、推理徽章、当前选中高亮，加载 / 失败 / 会话占用等状态都有清晰呈现。
**选择模型后立即回写模型下拉框并生效** —— 因为它与原生下拉框共用同一条
per-session 模型目录与 `selectModel` 提交路径（"任一端切换，另一端立刻显示"）。

## 效果

![模型速选窗口（深色主题，中文界面）](screenshot_zh.png)

![模型下拉左侧的触发按钮](button.png)

- **触发按钮**：28px 圆形图标按钮，紧贴模型下拉左侧，与 composer 工具栏
  「+」按钮同风格（悬停 / 焦点环 / 禁用态齐全）。
- **选择窗口**（居中弹窗，主题变量配色，深浅色主题自适应）：
  - **头部**：标题 + 提供商/模型计数 + 关闭；
  - **最近使用**：打开即见上次用过的模型（最多 8 个，自动记录、本地持久化），
    每行显示 **`提供商 · 模型`**（如 `火山方舟 · deepseek-v4-flash-ga`），
    点一下即切回常用模型；
  - **提供商筛选**：搜索框左侧的自定义下拉（全部提供商 / 单个提供商），
    跟随主题渲染（不用原生 `<select>`，避免深色主题下系统面板惨白）；
  - **搜索**：模型名 / 模型 id / 提供商名模糊匹配，↑↓ 移动高亮、Enter 选中、Esc 关闭；
  - **列表**：按提供商分组（DeepSeek 账号 / 官方优先），分组带色条与计数徽章，
    每行显示 **完整模型名** + **能力标签** + 「推理」徽章 + 「当前」徽章 + 选中勾，
    大列表按需懒渲染（滚动才加载，打开更快）；
  - **底部**：当前模型摘要 + **推理档位（reasoning effort）选择器** + 关闭按钮；
  - **状态**：加载中（spinner）、加载失败（重试）、提供商加载失败（逐条提示）、
    当前模型已不可路由（警告）、会话被占用（专用文案）。

### 能力标签是真实数据

行内的 `📝 文本` / `🖼️ 图像` 标签**不是**从模型描述文字里猜的，而是读
**用户自己配置里声明的 `input` 列表**（pi-ai 提供商配置，如
`providers.<id>.models[].input: [text, image]`）。实现走 DSH 已有的
`settings` Remote 读取 settings 文档，扫描各命名空间的 `providers → models[].input`
建索引；配置里没写 `input` 的提供商就不显示标签（如实反映配置，不做臆测）。
增删配置里的 `input`，标签随之变化。

> **契约说明（已验证）**：能力标签用 `group.id` 查询索引，而 `group.id` 与
> settings 中 `providers` 的**配置 key 同命名空间**（DSH 的 modelCatalog 以
> `provider.id` 作为分组 id、`provider.name` 作为显示名）。因此
> `providers.volcengine-agent-plan` 这类配置 key 能被可靠匹配；若未来 DSH
> 改变这一命名约定，标签会安静地不显示（不会报错），插件其余功能不受影响。

> **为什么只能从配置读（已验证）**：浏览器侧拿到的 `modelCatalog` RPC 返回的
> 模型对象**只有 `id` / `name` / `description` / `reasoning`，不含 `input`** ——
> DSH 的 Host 侧在构建浏览器目录时把 `input` 字段投影丢弃了（见
> `buildModelCatalog`）。因此插件无法从模型目录兜底读取能力，配置是浏览器侧
> 唯一的 `input` 来源。想给某个模型显示能力标签，就在 pi-ai 提供商配置里为它
> 写 `input`：
>
> ```yaml
> # profile 的 cordis.patch.yml，llm-pi-ai 提供商配置内
> models:
>   - id: deepseek-v4-flash-ga-260731
>     input: [text, image]   # 声明后插件即显示「文本 / 图像」标签
> ```
>
> 这也解释了为什么**同一个模型 id 在不同用户那里标签可能不同**——它如实反映
> 各自配置，而非模型本身的客观能力。

## 工作原理

1. 注册进 composer 的 **`conversation.input.right`** slot —— 这是一个
   `kind: list`、`scope: session` 的官方扩展点，composer 栏在渲染模型
   seat（`conversation.input.model`）之前渲染它，因此按钮天然出现在
   模型下拉的**左边**。
2. 通过 `ctx.inject(['slots', 'modelDirectories'], …)` 拿到
   `ctx.modelDirectories`（由 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-model-selection`
   注册的共享服务），对当前会话解析出与原生下拉**同一个**
   `ModelDirectory` 实例。
3. 弹窗里选择模型 → `directory.select({ provider, model, reasoningEffort })`
   → 走与原生下拉完全相同的 `selectModel` RPC。成功后共享 store 更新，
   原生模型下拉的标签**自动回写**，会话模型切换立即生效。
4. 能力标签由 `ctx.inject(['…', 'remote', 'remote.settings'])` 注入的
   `settings` Remote 读取：`settings.describe()` 返回各命名空间的合并配置，
   从中提取 `provider → model → input[]`。注意 **`remote.<namespace>` 必须显式
   写进 inject 列表**（cordis 规则），只注入根 `remote` 会在访问时报
   `cannot get property "remote.settings" without inject`。
5. 子代理（subagent addressed）会话没有模型目录，按钮自动隐藏。

## 安装

支持 **web 与 desktop** 两个 profile（`platform: web` 的插件在两者中均生效）。

### 方式 A：git clone 后本地安装（推荐）

```sh
git clone https://github.com/faxble/dsh-model-picker.git
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-model-picker
```

把 `/path/to/dsh-model-picker` 换成实际 clone 路径；桌面版把 `web` 换成
`desktop`：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /path/to/dsh-model-picker
```

安装后重启 DeepSeek Harness，在「设置 → 插件」中启用 `dsh-model-picker`，
或确认它已自动启用。

### 方式 B：远程直接安装（免 clone）

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:faxble/dsh-model-picker
```

### 方式 C：手动加入 profile（开发者调试用）

1. 在 profile（默认 `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop`）的 `package.json` 中：
   - `dependencies` 增加 `"dsh-model-picker": "file:D:\\Dev\\VibeCoding\\dsh-model-picker"`；
   - `dsh.profile.bundles` 增加 `"dsh-model-picker"`。
2. 在 profile 目录执行 `pnpm install`。
3. 重启 DeepSeek Harness。

## 目录结构

```
dsh-model-picker/
├── package.json        # 包元数据 + dsh.client 声明（platform: web）
├── index.js            # Host 半身（no-op，仅承载 bundle 行）
├── cordis.patch.yml    # bundle patch：一行 insert（name 为裸包名）
├── client.js           # 浏览器半身：ModuleLoader bundle（由 src/ 构建）
├── install.ps1         # 安装脚本（web / desktop）
├── src/                # 源码（ES modules，开发用）
│   ├── dict.js         #   zh/en 文案字典
│   ├── pure.js         #   纯逻辑：排序/搜索打分/MRU/能力标签（单测覆盖）
│   ├── style.js        #   CSS（主题变量）
│   ├── icons.js        #   SVG 图标
│   └── entry.js        #   ModuleLoader bundle 入口（组件 + apply）
├── scripts/build.mjs   # esbuild 打包脚本
├── test/               # node:test 单元测试
└── README.md
```

## 说明

- 纯前端插件：**运行时无构建、无运行时依赖**（只用 shell 已提供的 `react`），
  全部颜色来自 DSH 主题 CSS 变量，切换深浅色主题无需重载。
  `client.js` 是构建产物，开发期用 `pnpm build` 从 `src/` 生成。
- 不修改任何 DSH 核心代码；`conversation.input.right` 目前没有任何占用者，
  注册不会遮蔽既有 UI。
- 界面文案**中英双语**，随 DSH 系统语言自动切换（zh / en），外国用户可直接使用。
- 附加功能：**最近使用（MRU）置顶**、**搜索打分排序**（精确 > 前缀 > 包含）、
  **推理档位（reasoning effort）选择器**、大列表**懒渲染**、焦点陷阱等无障碍支持。
  - 最近使用行显示 **`提供商 · 模型`**（如 `火山方舟 · deepseek-v4-flash-ga`），
    提供商名在模型左侧、本地化并浅灰次要显示，跨提供商时避免同名模型混淆。
- 主题取值注意：**不要用 `--dsw-alias-brand-text` 做选中行文字色** ——
  它的语义是"品牌色块**上**的文字"（浅色主题设计值），深色主题下解析为深色，
  配软高亮底会变成黑字看不清；文字统一用 `--dsw-alias-label-primary`。

## 开发调试

- 改 `src/` 后执行 `pnpm build` 重新生成 `client.js`，再复制到 profile 触发
  HMR 热更新（页面无需刷新，DSH 会检测到文件变更并重新加载 bundle）：

  ```powershell
  pnpm build
  Copy-Item .\client.js $env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-model-picker\client.js -Force
  ```

- 单元测试：`pnpm test`（`node --test`，覆盖 `src/pure.js` 的纯逻辑）。
- 构建校验：`pnpm check`（`node --check` 产物）。**CI 会校验 `client.js` 是否为
  最新构建**，改了 `src/` 忘了 build 会让 CI 失败。
- 若要源码改动即时生效（免复制），改用 `link:` 符号链接方式安装。
- 移除插件：DSH「设置 → 插件」里卸载 `dsh-model-picker` 即可。

plugins.description: Export DeepSeek Harness (dsh) sessions as readable Markdown. Pick individual messages from one session, or merge several into a single .md / split them into a ZIP.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-session-md-export 把 DeepSeek Harness（`dsh`）的会话导出成**可读的 Markdown**。 Harness 自带的导出（`/export`、会话菜单里的「下载 Session 日志」）给的是一个装着**原始 JSONL 日志**的 ZIP—— 那是给回放和排查用的，不是给人读的。这个插件补上缺的那一半：把会话折成**轮次 + 条目**的对话记录， 渲染成 Markdown 文档。 | 需求 | 这个插件怎么做 | | --- | --- | | 导出成 md | 每个会话渲染成一份 Markdown：YAML front matter（机器可读）+ 标题 + 元信息表 + 目录 + 逐轮逐条正文 | | 单会话可选内容 | 选中一个会话后进入逐条挑选：每一轮、每一条（用户 / 助手 / 工具调用 / 工具结果 / 注入上下文 / 系统提示 / 流程记录）都能单独勾选 | | 多会话合并或分开 | 选中多个会话后由你决定：**合并**成一个 `.md`，或**分开**导出成 `.zip`（每个会话一个文件，外加一份索引 `README.md`） | ## 界面 侧栏 → **设置** → **Markdown 导出**。三步： ### 第 1 步 · 选择会话 按工作区分组的全部会话（标题、最近活动、占用大小、会话 id），可按标题 / 会话 ID / 工作目录筛选， 有全选与清空。 - 勾选**一个** → 下一步是逐条挑选内容。 - 勾选**多个** → 下一步是按类别统一选择，再下一步决定合并还是分开。 ### 第 2 步 · 选择内容 **单会话**：每一轮一个分组，每一条一行——复选框 + 类型 + 工具名 + `#seq` + 字符数 + 内容预览。 另有按类别的批量开关（`用户 4/4`、`工具调用 42/42` 这种），组内也有全选。 **默认只勾选「你问的」和「助手答的」**——也就是问答本身： | 类别 | 默认 | 是什么 | | --- | --- | --- | | 🧑 用户 | **开** | 你提的问题 | | 🤖 助手 | **开** | 助手给你的回答（**不含**思考过程与工具调用） | | 🔧 工具调用 | 关 | 助手请求调用的工具与参数——属于「自言自语」 | | 📤 工具结果 | 关 | 工具返回的内容，通常是日志或文件正文——属于「自言自语」 | | 📥 注入上下文 | 关 | DSH 自动注入的运行上下文、技能目录等 | | ⚙️ 系统提示 | 关 | 系统提示词，即助手收到的初始指令 | | • 流程记录 | 关 | 压缩、命令等流程记录 | **思考过程**另有独立开关（默认关），它也不是「助手答的」，而是助手给自己的推理。 > 为什么默认这么窄：三类被排除的东西——工具调用、工具结果、思考过程——都是助手**为自己**产生的， > 不是它给你看的东西；而它们的篇幅远超对话本身。实测一个会话：1404 条里只有 443 条是问答， > 默认导出 47 KB，全选则 2.3 MB。想要过程的话，上面的类别开关就在旁边，一下就能打开。 > > 注意「工具调用」关掉**不会**让工具调用的内容消失：助手条目里内嵌的那份也不会再渲染， > 因为在导出里工具调用本来就由它自己那一行负责——早先两个地方都渲染，导致每条命令在文件里 > 出现两次（实测某个参数串重复了 33 次）。打开该类别，它只出现一次，在那行自己的标题下。 **多会话**：按类别统一开关，应用到选中的每个会话，并显示各自的命中条数。 （跨会话逐条勾选不是真实工作流，所以这里不假装提供。） ### 第 3 步 · 导出方式 多会话时是两张互斥的卡片，各自写明**会得到什么文件**： | 选择 | 结果 | | --- | --- | | **合并为一个文件** | 一个 `.md`，每个会话一个 `##` 分节。适合整体阅读或全文搜索。 | | **分开为单文件（ZIP）** | 一个 `.zip`，里面每个会话一份 `.md`（`01 标题.md`、`02 标题.md`…）外加索引 `README.md`。 | 还有 **Markdown 预览**：不下载，先在弹窗里看一眼实际会生成什么。 ## 输出长什么样 ````markdown --- title: "会话标题" session_id: "session-00000000-1111-2222-3333-444444444444" cwd: "C:\\workspace\\my-project" created_at: "2026-01-16 20:40:38" exported_at: "2026-01-16 21:02:03" exporter: "dsh-session-md-export" session_format_version: 4 turns: "1" items: 254 omitted_items: 1180 tool_calls: 0 tokens: "in 6643, out 12718" --- # 会话标题 | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | Session | `session-00000000-1111-2222-3333-444444444444` | | Working directory | `C:\workspace\my-project` | | Turns | 1 | | Items | 254 | | Tool calls | 0 | | Span | 2026-01-16 20:45:06 → 2026-01-16 21:02:01 (16m 56s) | | Omitted | 1180 item(s) not in this export | ## Turn 1 *2026-01-16 20:45:06 · 16m 56s* ### 🧑 User *2026-01-16 20:45:06* 帮我看看这个模块，然后补一份说明文档。 ### 🤖 Assistant (108 out) *2026-01-16 20:45:08* I'll start by understanding the plugin system. ### 🤖 Assistant (250 out) *2026-01-16 20:45:12* Let me explore the plugin architecture. ### 🤖 Assistant (410 out) *2026-01-16 20:45:23* Here is what I found: the module does X, and the documentation is below. ```` 上面这份就是**默认设置**的产物：只有问答。注意第三段助手消息其实是「调用了工具、然后根据结果作答」—— 默认导出里只留下它给你的那段答案，中间那些工具调用与日志不会挤进来。 把类别开关打开后，同一份导出会多出这些（每条工具调用只出现一次，不再在助手段落里重复）： ````markdown ### 🤖 Assistant (108 out, 160 reasoning) *2026-01-16 20:45:08*
Reasoning ```text The user wants me to look at the module. ```
I'll start by understanding the plugin system. ### 🔧 Tool call — `pwsh` *2026-01-16 20:45:08* Call id: `call_00_j4Ax36cQ3gmJLxsHVJxm1707` ```json { "command": "pwd", "description": "Show working directory" } ``` ### 📤 Tool result — `pwsh` *2026-01-16 20:45:08* Call id: `call_00_j4Ax36cQ3gmJLxsHVJxm1707` ```text /workspace/my-project ``` ```` 三条渲染规则值得说明： 1. **助手正文按 Markdown 原样输出**，它自己的标题、列表、代码块都保留； 2. **工具参数与工具输出一律加围栏**——它们是任意文本，常常自带三个反引号。围栏长度会自动比内容里 最长的一段反引号多一个，所以内容永远撑不破围栏、不会污染后文； 3. **附件不会被静默丢掉**：图片 / 文件会渲染成带 attachment id 的引用，说明「未嵌入本次导出」。 思考过程放在 `
` 折叠块里（正文外），默认关闭，可在第 2 步的「包含思考过程」打开。 **一个只有工具调用、没有正文的助手回合会被整段略过**，而不是留下一个空标题或占位说明—— 实测某会话 648 个助手回合里有 252 个是这样，逐条写「此处省略」只会给正文加几百行噪音。 省略的总量已经在文档里说明：front matter 的 `omitted_items` 和元信息表的 `Omitted` 一行。 ## 安装 两种方式二选一。**装完都需要完全退出并重启 DSH**（组合包那一行不会热加载）， 再按 `Ctrl+Shift+R` 硬刷新页面。 > 本插件**没有发布到 npm**，所以「只填包名」（例如直接填 `dsh-session-md-export`）会失败—— > 请用下面的 GitHub 地址或本地路径。 ### 方式一：在界面里装（推荐） DSH 自带插件管理器，不需要开命令行。 **1. 打开插件页** 侧栏 → **插件**。页面分「官方」与「已安装」两组。 **2. 点「添加插件」** 在页面里点 **添加插件**，弹出对话框。输入框的标签是 **包名或地址**（提示文字写着 「输入插件的包名、GitHub 仓库地址或本地目录路径」）。 **3. 填入 GitHub 地址** ``` github:vi0let-dev/dsh-session-md-export ``` 输入框下方有个可展开的 **插件安装引导和示例**；对话框里也说明了：包名就是本 README 里 `dsh plugin add` 后面那一段。这里填的是 `github:` 开头的仓库地址，**不是**裸包名。 想装本地目录（自己改代码、改完即时生效）就改填绝对路径： ``` D:\src\dsh-session-md-export ``` **4. 点「安装」** 按钮会依次变成 **正在检查…** → **正在准备安装…** → **插件安装中…**， 中途可以展开 **查看安装详情** 看 pnpm 的实时输出。装完显示 **已安装**。 > 如果卡在 GitHub：对话框会出现 **无法访问 GitHub** 或 **连接 GitHub 超时**， > 并给出 **改用国内镜像**。注意镜像只代理 npm 源，**不代理 GitHub 仓库下载**—— > 本插件只以 GitHub 分发，所以那条路走不通时要靠本机网络或代理访问 GitHub。 **5. 点「立即启用」** 安装完成后对话框会给出 **立即启用**。点它会把这个组合包加入 profile 并启用。 **直接关掉对话框则它会保持「已安装但未启用」**——那种状态下插件不会运行， 侧栏里也不会出现它的入口。 顺便确认一下 profile 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里有 `dsh-session-md-export` （`%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\package.json`）。「立即启用」会自己写进去； 万一没写，手动补一行再重启： ```jsonc { "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ "@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "dsh-session-md-export" // ← 必须有这一行，否则 Host 侧不会被加载 ] } } } ``` **6. 完全退出并重启 DSH，然后硬刷新** 组合包那一行只在启动时加载，所以**必须重启宿主**，光刷新页面没用。 重启后按 `Ctrl+Shift+R`。打开 **设置 → Markdown 导出** 应该能看到本插件的页面。 ### 方式二：命令行 ```powershell # 从 GitHub 直装（推荐：装到 profile 自己的 node_modules） dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:vi0let-dev/dsh-session-md-export # 锁定版本（tag 或 commit） dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:vi0let-dev/dsh-session-md-export#v1.0.0 # 本地目录：装成软链，改代码立即生效 dsh plugin --profile desktop add "D:\src\dsh-session-md-export" ``` `--profile` 填你实际在用的那个：桌面端默认 `desktop`，`dsh web` 是 `web`。 装完同样确认 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里有这一行，然后重启 + 硬刷新。 > ⚠️ 两种装法的差别值得记一下：**GitHub 直装是副本**（换了代码要重新 add 一次才生效）， > **本地目录是软链**（指向你的工作副本）。用软链时不要用 `Remove-Item -Recurse` 去删 > profile 里的 `node_modules\dsh-session-md-export`——那可能顺着链接删到你项目里的东西； > 要摘链接用 `cmd /c rmdir "\node_modules\dsh-session-md-export"`。 ### 装完没出现入口？ 1. 确认插件启用后**重启**了 DSH，并按 `Ctrl+Shift+R` 硬刷新过； 2. 确认装进了你正在用的那个 profile（插件页顶部会显示它管理的 profile）； 3. 打开 **设置**，看导航里有没有 **Markdown 导出**； 4. 还不行就看 Host 日志有没有 `session-md-export: routes mounted at …`—— 没有的话多半是 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里缺那一行。 ## 环境要求 - DeepSeek Harness **0.2.0-rc.2** 桌面端或 `dsh web`。 - Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`（随 DSH 自带的即可）。 会话日志是 **Zstandard** 压缩的，`node:zlib` 的 zstd 支持是硬需求；缺了插件仍会加载， 但界面会明确告警、读不了日志。 - **无构建步骤、无第三方依赖**：ZIP 是自己按格式写的（`node:zlib` 之上）， `client.js` 是手写的 ModuleLoader bundle，只用外壳本来就提供的 `react`。 这样从 GitHub 直装不会撞上 pnpm 的 `allowBuilds` 构建授权拦截。 ## 会话日志是怎么读的 这一步有个坑，值得写下来，因为**朴素实现会读到空会话却毫无报错**。 `session.v4.jsonl.zstd` 不是**一个** zstd 流，而是一个**拼接帧容器**：持久化后端把每一批持久事件 各压成一个独立可解码、带校验和的帧，这样追加写入和尾部恢复都不必重读整个文件。 于是 `zstdDecompressSync(整个文件)` 只会解出**第一帧**——而第一帧恰好就是那**一行** header。 不明就里的人会以为这个会话是空的。 所以帧必须先按结构定位、再逐帧解码。`src/zstd.js` 里的扫描器按帧头与块头走字节， 不做解压（因此定位很便宜），校验和交给解码器。这与后端自己的 `scanZstdFrames` 一致。 **尾部残缺的帧是正常状态**（日志正在被追加），会用 `ZSTD_e_flush` 尽量抢救出已写入的部分。 会话内容是**直接读磁盘**的：`$DSH_HOME/sessions/<组>//session.v.jsonl[.zstd]`。 `ctx.sessionQuery` 更"正统"，但它只在挂了查询后端时才存在——一个在最小组合里会静默失效的导出工具， 比一个自己读格式的工具更糟。标题与 cwd 取自投影缓存 `storages/session_projcache/`（侧栏同源， 不必为了一个名字去解压日志）。工作区账本只读不写。 ## 一些行为细节 - **被替换（模型侧重写）的事件不入导出**。带 `surfaceOp: { op: 'replace' }` 的事件是模型侧的重写， `dsh-session` 明确说过折叠后的表层「不是人类转录的正确来源——落地的替换会抹掉用户已经看过的对话」。 所以它们被排除，并在界面上报出条数。 - **显式空选择会被尊重**。不传 `items` 表示「用默认」；传空数组表示「什么都不要」—— 两者是不同的意图，混为一谈会让用户刚清空的勾选又冒出来。空选择导出会得到一份写明 「未选择任何内容」的文档，而不是一份看起来正常其实没内容的文件。 - **会话 id 先过正则再拼路径**，扫不到日志的会话（账本里有登记、磁盘上没有）不会出现在列表里—— 它没有内容可导。 - **导出是纯读操作**：不会写任何会话、账本或项目文件。 - **多会话合并时每个会话仍是独立分节**（`## 1. 标题`），所以合并后的文件还能按标题重新拆开。 ## 安全边界 `/api/dsh-session-md-export/*` 只是一条**读**路由，但它能读到全部对话历史，所以三道闸： 1. **回环对端**：非回环连接直接 403； 2. **回环 `Host`**：挡 **DNS rebinding**——攻击者把域名解析到 127.0.0.1 后，那个请求对他自己的页面 来说是**同源**的，标志头也不会触发预检，此时 `Host` 不是回环字面量，因此被拒； 3. **标志头**

plugins.description: Time-shifting task delegation for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): plan tasks at leisure, they run unattended off-peak, come back to a report. Human-adjudicated, desktop + web.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-lowtide **Queue tasks when it's busy. They run on their own when it's cheap.** Semi-auto or full-auto, off the model's peak hours and peak prices. A must-have plugin for DeepSeek Harness. **English** | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) | [繁體中文](./README.zh-HK.md) | [العربية](./docs/README.ar.md) | [Deutsch](./docs/README.de.md) | [Español](./docs/README.es.md) | [Français](./docs/README.fr.md) | [Italiano](./docs/README.it.md) | [한국어](./docs/README.ko.md)
--- ![hero](./assets/screenshots/hero.png)

Three tasks waiting in the queue, the price status glowing in the session header, auto-run when your window opens

## Introduction lowtide is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (dsh)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh). The problem it solves is plain and perfectly natural: Usually, when you want an agent to do some work, you sit at the computer, send the agent an instruction, wait for the reply, and then review it by hand. But this workflow seems to forget that you have plenty of idle time — and a chance to dodge the peak/off-peak pricing that some models charge. With lowtide installed, the day goes like this: whenever a job crosses your mind during the day, toss it in the queue, glance at it, release it. The tasks pile up until the time you set (say, after 7 PM — that's when DeepSeek is at valley pricing), then run by themselves. Next morning you open the report: keep what went well, send back what didn't. That's all it is. But use it for a week and your working rhythm genuinely slows down — and don't forget, "time is money, efficiency is life"... A few key capabilities: - Four execution strategies: single, iterative, sampling, review — from "one pass is enough" to "run five candidates and I'll pick" - 168 unit tests + 10 end-to-end specs, CI green across ubuntu / windows × node 22 / 24 - One build artifact serves both desktop and web — install once, works on both - Off-peak execution lands in DeepSeek's valley hours: the same batch costs about half of what peak would ## A normal day with an agent might look like this… **Ten minutes before clocking out.** You've finished reviewing code, so you file three tickets for tomorrow: a refactor (iterative, 3 rounds), a weekly report (single), and a design you're unsure about (sampling, 4 candidates). Release them all, shut down, leave. Tomorrow at your desk, the morning report says: the refactor's done, the report's drafted, and four candidate designs sit side by side, each with its cost written out. **Friday night.** Queue a week's worth of chores in one go: dependency cleanup, missing tests, data scripts. Weekends are valley price around the clock. You go out; it works from home. Monday you check the report — retry what failed, merge what's good. **A 10 AM brainwave.** You're mid-conversation with the agent about an urgent bug when you think "hey, update the docs too." The intercept card pops up: running now costs peak price, tonight it's about half — the difference is spelled out. Click "queue for off-peak"; your draft survives untouched, and you go back to the bug. **An always-on server.** You've got a machine running dsh 24/7. Switch to L3 full-auto, then file tasks from anywhere through the API (`POST /ds-lowtide/tasks`). It runs them on schedule and writes the report. Nobody's watching, but the sandbox, the daily budget, and the file locks are all still there. **Deliverables for a client.** Use the review strategy: run once, then automatically open an independent session that tears the result apart through your chosen focus (say, "hunt for data-source errors"). In the morning you don't get a bare result — you get a result plus a critical review. **Living abroad.** You're in San Francisco; DeepSeek's peak is Beijing time, which for you lands in the evening and night before. Settings converts the official hours to your local clock, one click to adopt. You set windows by your own schedule, and the books always stay aligned with the official table. ## How lowtide works ``` ① Intake ② Adjudicate ③ Execute ④ Accept Whenever you have The queue dock When the off-peak When you're back: a moment: one-click groups tasks by window opens: five open the report — from the intercept workspace; triage preflight gates pass, results + diff card, or file a → line by line: → then sandboxed runs → + actual spend ticket (4 strategies) ✓approve ⏸defer one batch per window + money saved ✕drop / approve-all ``` A task's life: `pending-review → queued → preflight → running → done / failed / stale / timeout`, plus `deferred` (postponed) and `dropped` (soft-deleted, restorable). Step two is where lowtide differs from a "fully automated script": **every task must be released by your hand before it runs** (in L2, you release the whole batch at once, 30 minutes before the window). The machine cannot move itself into the run queue. Execution is automated; decisions are not. That's why you can safely be absent. ## A tour of the lowtide interface **The new-task modal.** Four strategies side by side, each with a plain-language hint; rounds, priority, and run mode ride along per task — no trip back to settings. Tasks land as "pending review". Nothing enters the queue without passing you. ![new-task-modal](./assets/screenshots/new-task-modal.png) **Advanced options.** Model, reasoning effort, priority from 0 to 9, fresh session or continue-previous, and the locked-files list — all in one small pane. Locked files, briefly: anything on the list gets sha256-checked before execution, and if it doesn't match what you filed, the task goes stale and refuses to run. Otherwise the file you queued against could be rewritten by another task while waiting, and this one would blindly stomp on it. ![advanced-options](./assets/screenshots/advanced-options.png) **Pick any model.** Batch runs default to the official `deepseek-flash` (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; the retired `deepseek-v4-flash` name still routes there at Flash prices), but each task can pick its own model — anything connected to your Harness is in the dropdown, grouped by provider. Private providers work too. Non-official models have no public price table, so the ledger honestly says "price unknown"; add a price override in settings if you want the bookkeeping exact. ![model-picker](./assets/screenshots/model-picker.png) **The window editor.** Multi-segment, overnight, per-weekday — all fine. Underneath is a live 24-hour price band: red for peak, green for valley, and a marker showing where you are right now. Outside UTC+8, one click on "adopt official peak hours" converts Beijing time to your local clock. ![window-editor](./assets/screenshots/window-editor.png) **The settings page.** Window hours, tasks per batch, per-task duration cap, concurrency, daily budget, report history, autonomy level, price overrides — all graphical, no config files. The official pricing rules (including the new all-weekend valley) are explained in human language on the same page. ![settings](./assets/screenshots/settings.png) Three more pieces of UI appear in daily use: the **price pill** (session header — busy/idle, queue size; click it to edit windows), the **peak-hours intercept card** (type at peak, it appears; the price difference is spelled out; your draft survives), and the **execution report** (the morning briefing: savings first, anomalies pinned, candidates awaiting your pick, one-click Markdown copy). ## About lowtide workspaces Every task runs inside a workspace. That single dropdown decides three things. **Which files it can touch.** Tasks run in a sandbox whose boundary is the workspace directory. Pick wrong and at best it can't find the files; at worst it edits something it shouldn't. **Who it queues with.** Tasks in the same workspace run serially (two tasks never fight over one repo); different workspaces run in paralle

plugins.description: DSH guard against self-repetition in streamed model output: detects a degeneration loop in reasoning or visible text, aborts the runaway turn and wakes the agent with a corrective notice.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-output-loop-guard

An **output self-repetition watchdog** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/).
When a model starts cycling the same short block instead of producing a tool call, the guard
aborts that generation and wakes the agent with a corrective notice — no human stop button,
and no human typing "continue".

- Bundle for DSH `>= 0.2.0-rc.2`, ESM, zero runtime dependencies.
- 21 self-contained regression checks (`npm test`).
- Calibrated against 27 real sessions / 1,783 assistant steps: **24 detections, 0 false positives**.

## The gap it fills

DSH ships `@deepseek-ai/dsh-repeat-tool-reminder`, which only sees **duplicate tool calls**
(same tool, same arguments, 3/5/8 times in a row). A degeneration loop in the *reasoning
channel* is invisible to it. In the session that motivated this plugin:

- the model repeated `好。→（执行）→好。→Write.→…` in its reasoning for **112,109 characters**,
  emitted in **50,196 stream chunks over 126 seconds of continuous decoding**, and produced
  **zero tool calls** — so `repeat-tool-reminder` could not fire;
- automatic compaction never ran either: its trigger is
  `floor(min(W × 0.8, W − O − B))` ≈ 678k tokens for a 1M window with a 256k output cap,
  while the session peaked around 508k tokens;
- the loop only ended when the human pressed stop, and the polluted text stayed in the
  transcript, which made further loops more likely (self-imitation).

`output-loop-guard` listens on the live `agent/assistant-stream` frames and looks at the text itself.

## How it works

A sliding window over streamed output (1,200 characters by default, inspected every 64 new
characters) feeds four signals:

| Signal | Rule | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| `repeated-block` | **Shortest-period** block (≥2 newlines, ≥2 distinct non-whitespace chars) repeated ≥6 times | Multi-line cycles, e.g. the 106-character `好。→（执行）→Write.` cycle |
| `dominant-gram` | One n-gram covers ≥55% of the window with ≥24 occurrences and spans ≥2 lines | Loops whose tail is ragged but where repetition already dominates |
| `repeated-line` | Single-line runs: ≥40 in the reasoning channel, ≥60 in visible text (`singleLineTextMinRepeats`, `0` disables) | Reasoning spinning on one line, runaway line duplication in answers |
| `flat-tic` | Whitespace-free short gram covering ≥25% of the window with ≥48 occurrences, **reasoning only** | Line-less tics (`好。好。好。…`) |

Two design rules keep it precise:

- **Only the shortest period counts.** When one line repeats, 2× and 3× the line length are also
  "periods"; judging on an arbitrary period turned an ordinary bullet list into a "multi-line
  cycle" during calibration. The guard therefore looks only at the shortest period and requires
  that block itself to span ≥2 newlines.
- **Channel awareness.** Repeated lines in visible output are usually legitimate content
  (generated fixtures, config files, lists), so the visible-text single-line threshold is higher
  (60) than the reasoning one (40), and line-less tics are only judged in the reasoning channel.
  Indentation runs, `====` / `----` rule lines and blank-line runs never trip the guard.

On detection the guard:

1. calls `agent.cancel({ kind: 'hook', reason: 'output-loop-guard: …' })` — the in-flight
   generation is aborted and recorded as interrupted, so the degenerate text stops growing;
2. calls `agent.steer(<notice>)` — because the signal is already aborted, `steer` upgrades to a
   **fresh turn** and wakes the driver, so the agent immediately continues with an explicit
   correction (stop restating, emit the next action or finish);
3. after `maxTripsPerTurn` trips in one turn it stops auto-continuing and only `inject`s the
   notice, so a genuinely broken model cannot spin forever.

## Install

The package is a DSH **bundle**: the loader reads `dsh.bundle.patch` from `package.json`
(`dsh.plugin.json` is optional metadata used by some local plugin indexes — the official runtime
ignores it), and `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the `output-loop-guard` row.

```sh
# A. from a git host, pinned to a commit (requires `git` on the PATH of the DSH process)
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add "github:ADistanceThereIs/dsh-output-loop-guard#<commit>"

# B. from the release tarball — no git required
#    download dsh-output-loop-guard-0.1.0.tgz from the Releases page, then:
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add ./dsh-output-loop-guard-0.1.0.tgz

# C. straight from the release asset URL (needs Node to trust your system CA store)
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add \
  https://github.com/ADistanceThereIs/dsh-output-loop-guard/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-output-loop-guard-0.1.0.tgz
```

All three append the package to `dsh.profile.bundles` and compose the bundle's patch layer.
**Restart DSH for the row to activate.**

Uninstall:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-output-loop-guard
```

## Configuration

Override the row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (a patch replaces the row's whole `config`,
so restate every key you want to keep):

```yaml
- id: output-loop-guard
  name: dsh-output-loop-guard
  config:
    dryRun: false                 # true = detect and log only, never cancel
    autoContinue: true            # wake the agent with the corrective notice
    maxTripsPerTurn: 2            # auto-continue budget per turn
    windowChars: 1200
    checkEveryChars: 64
    minPeriodRepeats: 6           # repeats required for a multi-line cycle
    singleLineMinRepeats: 40      # reasoning-channel single-line threshold
    singleLineTextMinRepeats: 60  # visible-text single-line threshold (0 = off)
    useDominantGram: true
    dominantGramCoverage: 0.55
    dominantGramMinCount: 24
    useFlatTic: true
    ticMinCount: 48
    ticMinCoverage: 0.25
    verbose: false
```

Start with `dryRun: true` if you want to observe detections in your own sessions before letting
the guard abort anything.

## Evidence

### Corpus calibration

Replayed over 27 real sessions / 1,783 assistant steps (a corpus containing both healthy and
degenerate real output):

- 24 detections, **0 false positives**;
- every loop step of the motivating session was caught, plus a same-pattern loop in an unrelated
  session;
- detection latency: the 112,109-character runaway was caught after **2,944 characters (2.6 %)**;
  other loops were caught within 1,152–7,808 characters — hundreds of milliseconds instead of
  20–126 seconds of spinning.

### Runtime verification

End-to-end check in a live DSH runtime, on a task engineered to repeat two lines 300 times. The
session log of that run contains:

```json
{"type":"turn/end","data":{"turn":1,"reason":{"kind":"aborted","reason":{"kind":"hook","reason":"output-loop-guard: repeated output (repeated-block)"}}}}
{"type":"assistant/message","interrupted":true}          // cut off after 9 repetitions, not 300
{"type":"user/message","source":{"kind":"output-loop-guard","form":"notice"}}
```

The agent then delivered the same content as a **file** instead of continuing to repeat it, which
is exactly the intended outcome: the guard stops runaway output, it does not kill the task.

### Regression suite

`npm test` runs 21 self-contained checks (no corpus needed): the real degeneracy must be aborted
(24,180-character stream caught after 576 characters), healthy long documents must be untouched,
realistic written output (lists, code blocks, tables, rule lines, fixtures) must not trip,
runaway written lines must trip, `dryRun` must not cancel, a disabled plugin must attach nothing,
and a throwing agent handle must not break the stream.

## Limitations

- Visible-text single-line repetition needs ≥60 identical consecutive lines (that protects
  legitimate fixtures and lists); disable with `singleLineTextMinRepeats: 0`.
- Detection is structural (periodicity and density), not semantic: a modified near-repeat may
  escape `repeated-block`, though `dominant-gram` / `flat-tic` usually covers it.
- Trips are counted per agent and per attempt; subagents do not share counters.
- A trip discards the tool call that step had not emitted yet — one retry is the price for not
  spinning for minutes. Use `dryRun` to observe first.
