--- **📖 Ecosystem knowledge base** — measured data, not marketing: [plugin development guide · plugin-selection data · maintenance criteria](https://perrylink.github.io/dsh-plugin-guide/). ## ⭐ 如果它帮到了你 这个插件是 [DSH 插件家族](https://github.com/PerryLink)的一员（40+ 个，全部 Apache-2.0）。如果你在用，**给个 star** —— 它不会解锁任何功能，但会让下一个人在搜索里更容易找到它。 *English:* part of a 40+ plugin family for DeepSeek Harness. If it is useful, **a star helps the next person find it** — nothing is gated behind it. ## What is dsh-permission-rules? Claude Code-style declarative permission rules for DeepSeek Harness. Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not. ![Terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules: dsh-permission-rules — deny/ask rules in one YAML file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.png) ![Animated terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.gif) *The same run, animated.* ## Compatibility | Surface | Status | |---|---| | Harness | DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1` (adapted 2026-09-22, full gate chain): its plugin config is the live settings contract — every field is declared `.volatile()`, the Loader hands `apply` a live reference per field, and a saved edit is committed into the running references WITHOUT remounting the plugin, with out-of-range values refused by the schema before anything is written. A host whose Schemastery predates `volatile()` (before 3.18.3) still mounts and runs this plugin — the fields simply stay ordinary values and the live config form is unavailable — because the marker is applied through a capability probe rather than assumed. `Session.append` on this line still cannot stamp the `ignorable` marker (its third argument is the surface-intent bag, and the envelope field survives for stored-log reads only), so the whole `0.2-alpha` line is pre-checked as unmarked and session-log audit stays disabled by default — `append` reads only `sourceEventSeqs`/`surfaceOp` and freezes the envelope, so it has no code path that could stamp the marker; the earlier `0.1.7-alpha` (adapted 2026-09-22), `0.1.5-rc.2` (adapted 2026-09-09) and `0.1.3-alpha` lines keep the same surface-only append signature, and every `0.2` prerelease is classified with them (a STABLE `0.2.x` release is left to the append probe, so a restored marker surface is adopted without a new plugin release). Those lines' log migrations refuse unclassified plugin events even when marked, so `strip` v1 audit rows before a `0.1.3-alpha` host opens the log and v2 audit rows before a `0.1.5-alpha` host migrates it (native v3 logs only need `repair`). | | Node | `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` | | Platforms | All (host + web settings client) | | Model | Any (deny/ask reasons surface through tool results) | ## What you get `dsh-permission-rules` puts an ordered **`allow` / `deny` / `ask`** rule list in front of every tool call on the `tools/pre-execute` waterfall — deterministic, instant, auditable, and written by you in plain YAML: - **`deny`** blocks the call; the rule's `reason` becomes the model-visible error. - **`ask`** rides the official approval seam (mount `dsh-auto-review` for a second-model answerer, or a human answers; with neither, the harness fails closed). - **`allow`** (and no-match) strictly delegates via `next()` — downstream listeners are never short-circuited. Every hit **and** every passthrough is audit-logged as a `permissionRules/decision` session event (log-only — nothing extra is injected into the model context). - **Rich matching** — tool-name globs (including `mcp__*`), agent-identity selectors (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:*`), argument key/value globs **or** regexes (with `!pattern` negation and an `absent` key dimension), workspace-relative path globs at **any nesting depth**, `when` host conditions (env vars, platform), and **shell command decomposition** (`argv`: command word, argument tokens, pipeline signature) for token-precise command matching. - **Built-in high-risk baseline** — a shipped deny/ask ruleset (destructive commands, privilege escalation, download-and-execute, sensitive paths) enabled by default and appended after user rules so a nearer user rule can override it; toggle with `builtin.enabled`. - **Hierarchical rule files** — optional `searchUp` merges every `.dsh/rules.yaml` from the session cwd to the filesystem root, nearest first. - **Dry-run rollout** — `enforce: false` audits what the policy *would* do while passing every call through. - **Hot reload** — Chokidar watch with debounce; a broken edit keeps the previous rules, never crashes. On a WSL host, or for a rule file under `/mnt/`, the watch switches to polling because native change events are unreliable there. - **Fail loud** — invalid YAML, unknown actions/fields, bad globs/regexes, backtracking-prone patterns, or more than `maxRules` rules fail the load. ## Rule syntax ```yaml # /.dsh/rules.yaml rules: - match: { tools: [bash, pwsh], params: { command: "git push*" }, paths: ["**/secrets/**"] } action: deny reason: "No pushes from protected paths" - match: { tools: [edit, write] } action: ask reason: "File writes need confirmation" ``` - **Match dimensions** — `tools` (globs, incl. `mcp__*`), `agents` (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:`; unknown identity never matches — fail closed), `params` (key/value globs or regexes, `!pattern` negation, `absent` key dimension), `paths` (workspace-relative globs extracted at any nesting depth), `when` (`env` var globs/regexes + a closed `platform` list), and `network` (`domains` / `ips` / `ports` / `schemes` — globs, wildcards, CIDRs, port ranges). - **Actions** — `allow` / `deny` / `ask`, evaluated in file order, first match wins. - **Rule metadata** — `enabled: false` (visible but inert), `description`, `tags`; unknown fields fail the load. - **Schema**

plugins.description: 自研 DeepSeek Harness (dsh) 插件集合 — 目前收录 dsh-auto-upgrade：Web UI 自动检测升级 + 兼容性预检 + 一键备份/安装/校验/重启
plugins.readme_text:
# self-dsh-plugins

自研 / 自维护 / fork 来的 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai)（`dsh`）插件集合。
每个子目录是一个独立插件，通过 profile 的 `link:` 依赖挂到本机 DSH 上使用；**不走 npm 发布流程**。

## 插件清单

| 目录 | 包名 | 作用 | 状态 |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`dsh-auto-upgrade/`](./dsh-auto-upgrade) | `dsh-plugin-auto-upgrade` | dsh Web UI 自升级：检测 → 兼容性预检 → 非阻塞浮层 → 一键备份 / 安装 / 校验 / 重启 | 可用（真机升级链路待验证） |
| [`dsh-external-discuss/`](./dsh-external-discuss) | `dsh-plugin-external-discuss` | 把 DSH 会话一键送到外部模型（清言网页版）继续讨论 | 可用（需配套 Chrome 扩展；仅清言接通） |
| [`dsh-im-bridge-workspaces/`](./dsh-im-bridge-workspaces) | `@mhfire/dsh-im-bridge` | 企业微信智能机器人 ⇄ DSH Agent 桥接，本地 fork 增加多工作区 `/ws` 切换 | 可用（本机已接入 profile） |
| [`dsh-plugin-product-subagents/`](./dsh-plugin-product-subagents) | `dsh-plugin-product-subagents` | 把 Claude Code / Codex / 任意 ACP CLI 变成基于角色的 subagent（`0.2.0` 线可续接；`0.2.1+` 外部子代理为一次性） | 可用（DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` / `0.2.1-alpha.5` / `0.2.1-rc.1` 均通过一次性 profile 验收） |

---

## dsh-auto-upgrade

**来源：纯原创**（`package.json` 的 `repository` 已指向本仓库 `directory: dsh-auto-upgrade`）。
**改动：—**（没有上游）。

给 dsh 的 Web UI 加一个**自升级**入口：当天首次打开页面时自动检测 dsh 新版本与已装插件的兼容性，
用一个**不打断当前工作**的浮层提示；用户点「升级」后才走完整链路。

![设置页](./dsh-auto-upgrade/docs/screenshots/settings.png)

![浮层](./dsh-auto-upgrade/docs/screenshots/overlay.png)

### 它做什么

1. **当天首次打开自动检测**：宿主按本地日期幂等，同一天多标签页 / 刷新只真正检测一次。
2. **检测两件事**：npm 上的 dsh 新版本；已装插件对**目标版本**的兼容性（用官方 `evaluatePluginCompatibility`，不是自己写范围匹配）。
3. **不打断工作的浮层**：右下角卡片，只占自己的位置；可「稍后」「不再提示」。
4. **点升级才动手**：会话门禁 → 插件门禁 → 备份 `~/.dsh` → 停服 → `npm install -g` → 对版 + 组合冒烟 → 重启交接。
5. **回滚与重启**：重装指定旧版本；或只重启服务。设置页还有本机体检、插件兼容表、升级 / 重启日志。

### 关键设计

- **双面插件，无构建步骤**：宿主半边 `lib/index.js` 用 cordis 注册 `/api/dsh-auto-upgrade/*` 路由族；
  浏览器半边 `lib/client.js` 手写并包在 `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory})` 里，注册
  `shell.overlay` 浮层与 `settings.section` 设置页。
- **变更必须脱离进程**：`npm install -g` 覆盖的正是宿主此刻在运行的那棵树，而「停服」就是杀掉宿主自己。
  所以宿主只做「门禁 → 备份 → 落 payload → fork detached helper → `exit 0`」，停服 / 安装 / 对版 / 冒烟 / 拉起
  都在生成的 POSIX sh helper 里。
- **故意不声明 `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peerDependencies**：否则升级之后，平台闸门会把「负责升级 dsh 的插件」
  自己判成不兼容（自锁）。本包只声明 `react`（浏览器半边需要）。
- **安全边界**：路由族能读 npm、重写全局安装树、覆盖 `~/.dsh`、结束本进程，所以一律 loopback-only
  （以 socket 地址为准，不信任 `X-Forwarded-For`），并且**有副作用的一律 POST**。
- **UI 吃 dsh 的设计 token**：字体 `--dsw-font-*`、圆角 `--dsw-radius-*`、语义色 `--dsw-alias-state-*`，
  数值逐条对齐官方实现。详见包内 README 的「UI 风格契约」。

### 两条门禁（默认策略）

| 情况 | 行为 |
|---|---|
| 有会话正在执行 | `409`，前端弹警告；用户确认后可带 `force` 继续（**仅警告**） |
| 目标版本与已装插件不兼容 | `409`，**拒绝升级且不可绕过**——先升级 / 移除那个插件，或为它写精确版本豁免 |

> 豁免是按「插件@版本 → dsh 版本」精确匹配的：为 `0.2.0-rc.2` 写的豁免，升级到别的版本时**自动失效**，
> 那个插件会立刻出现在「不兼容」里。这正是本插件要提前告诉你的信息。

### 已知限制（诚实清单）

- **真机的安装 / 升级 / 重启链路尚未执行**（属于需要用户点头的闸门）；只读半边与门禁已在真机验证。
- 只支持 macOS / Linux：helper 是 POSIX sh 脚本。
- `POST /plugins/action`（写豁免 / 禁用插件）尚未接线，如实返回 `501`；`GET /notes` 已实现。
- 暂不做「静默自动升级」：`policy.mode` 只接受 `notify`。

### 文档

- [设计：接口清单 + 数据流图 + 拍板结论](./dsh-auto-upgrade/docs/design/dsh-auto-upgrade-T1.md)
- [验收报告：逐条证据 + 明确没验证什么](./dsh-auto-upgrade/docs/acceptance/dsh-auto-upgrade-acceptance.md)
- 面向 agent 的工作约定：[`docs/plugins/dsh-auto-upgrade.md`](./docs/plugins/dsh-auto-upgrade.md)

---

## dsh-external-discuss

**来源：纯原创**。**改动：—**（没有上游）。

在助手消息操作栏（复制 / 反馈 / 新对话分支 / 用量 / 时间那一条）多出一个图标按钮，点开弹层选择投递目标：

| 目标 | 状态 | 行为 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 清言（`chatglm.cn`） | ✅ 可用 | 在已登录的清言页新建对话 → 按 DSH 会话标题重命名 → 粘贴正文 → 发送 |
| 千问 / DeepSeek | ⏸ 占位 | 显示「即将支持」，不可点 |

链路：页面按钮 → `GET /api/dsh-external-discuss/payload?sessionId=…`（宿主取正文与标题，
取自 `session.deriveMessages()` 的会话投影，不是抓页面 DOM）→ `window.postMessage` →
配套 Chrome 扩展转发到清言标签页 → 回执逐级回投 → 按钮下方显示结果。

安装分两步：插件（`dsh plugin --profile web add`，装完重启 dsh web）+ Chrome 扩展
（`chrome://extensions` → 开发者模式 → 加载已解压的扩展程序 → 选 `extension/`，装完**刷新 DSH 页面**）。
清言是第三方页面，改版会让选择器失效——候选文本集中在 `extension/qingyan-content.js` 顶部的 `CONFIG` 里。
详见 [包内 README](./dsh-external-discuss/README.md) 与 [`docs/plugins/dsh-external-discuss.md`](./docs/plugins/dsh-external-discuss.md)。

---

## dsh-im-bridge-workspaces

**来源：fork** 自 npm 包 `@mhfire/dsh-im-bridge@0.4.4`（本地 fork 版本 `0.4.4-ws.1`），
上游原版说明见 [README.upstream.md](./dsh-im-bridge-workspaces/README.upstream.md)。

**改了什么：** 新增**工作区列表与 `/ws` 切换**（`/ws`、`/ws <序号|title|路径|id>`、`/ws reset`、
`/ws add <路径>`、`/ws help`，以及 `workspaceSwitch` / `workspaceAllowFrom` / `workspaceAdd` 三个配置项
与 `$DSH_HOME/dsh-im-bridge/workspace-bindings.json` 持久化）；**其余行为与上游一致**——按企微窗口建 Agent、
单聊一人一条、群聊共用一条、Settings 配置卡片、wecom-cli 办公层均未改。

包名与目录名不同（目录 `dsh-im-bridge-workspaces/` → 包名 `@mhfire/dsh-im-bridge`），fork 保持同名，
所以接入 profile 时 `bundle` 列表与 `cordis.patch.yml` 都不用改。
这是本仓库**唯一需要构建**的插件（`src/` → `lib/`，`pnpm run build`）。
详见 [包内 README](./dsh-im-bridge-workspaces/README.md) 与
[`docs/plugins/dsh-im-bridge-workspaces.md`](./docs/plugins/dsh-im-bridge-workspaces.md)。

---

## dsh-plugin-product-subagents

**来源：fork** 自 GitHub `shaokeyibb/dsh-plugin-product-subagents` v0.4.0，
commit `e5a002db3b8d6df984fdb5e704e9321dca1723cd`，MIT。

**改了什么（适配 DSH `0.2.x`，业务代码未改）：**

- 扩展 `peerDependencies` / `dsh.compatibility.dsh` 的 DSH 版本范围，补 `dshReleases` verdict
  （`0.2.0-rc.2`、`0.2.1-rc.1`，**均有一次性 profile 验收背书**：install · compose · start · uninstall）；
- 版本 `0.4.0 → 0.4.1`，同步 `CHANGELOG.md` / `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` / `README.md` + `README.zh.md`；
- 并入本仓库统一管理（**已删除其内层 `.git`**，上游历史见上述 commit）。

> 为什么只改声明：0.4.0 在 `0.2.x` 上其实已能正常运行，缺的只是声明——
> DSH 启动时按插件**自己声明的** peer 范围判兼容，没覆盖就跳过该 bundle（表现为「插件莫名其妙没加载」）。
> ⚠️ prerelease 陷阱：`^0.2.0-rc.2` **不覆盖** `0.2.1-rc.1`，每条 `0.2.x` 线都要单独写一个锚点。

它把 Claude Code / Codex / 任意 ACP CLI 变成基于角色的可续接 subagent：一次性同步或异步可续接、
持久会话恢复、每角色 product 权限、受**权限天花板**约束的委派、声明式角色库（`roles/*.json`）。
详见 [英文 README](./dsh-plugin-product-subagents/README.md) / [中文 README](./dsh-plugin-product-subagents/README.zh.md) /
[`docs/plugins/dsh-plugin-product-subagents.md`](./docs/plugins/dsh-plugin-product-subagents.md)。

---

## 环境要求

| 项 | 要求 |
|---|---|
| DSH | `0.2.0-rc.2`（本机实测版本）；插件各自声明兼容范围，见上 |
| Node | `v24.21.0`（各插件 `engines` 不一，`dsh-auto-upgrade` / `dsh-external-discuss` 要求 `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.0.0`，`dsh-plugin-product-subagents` 要求 `>=18`） |
| 包管理器 | **pnpm**（本仓库与全局约定一律 pnpm，禁 npm / yarn / bun / npx；详见 [`AGENTS.md`](./AGENTS.md) 强制规定 2） |
| 产品 CLI | `dsh-plugin-product-subagents` 至少需要 `claude` / `codex` / 任一 ACP CLI 之一（如本机的 `opencode`） |
| shell | macOS 自带 bash 3.2（脚本已按 3.2 写） |

## 安装 / 卸载

```sh
# 安装（<目录> 用仓库内的目录名，路径按实际 clone 位置调整）
dsh plugin --profile web add /Users/gubin/workspace/self-dsh-plugins/<目录>

# 卸载
dsh plugin --profile web remove <包名>
```

- `add` 时若插件 `package.json` 声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch`，会自动挂上 patch 层，**无需手改**
  `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`。
- 本机 profile 是 `patchReload: live`：装完 / 改完通常**不用重启**，刷新页面即可。
  （`dsh-external-discuss` 与 `dsh-im-bridge-workspaces` 的宿主半边在冷启动装配，按各自 README 的说明处理。）
- `dsh plugin` 的 profile 目录在 `~/.dsh/profiles/web`；`dependencies` 用 `link:` 指向本仓库子目录。
- ⚠️ **改了 `link:` 目标路径后，必须在 `~/.dsh/profiles/web` 跑一次 `pnpm install`**，否则软链悬空、
  插件加载失败。

## 验证

```sh
# 跑 4 个插件的测试 / check / typecheck（缺 node_modules 的插件会明确跳过，不算失败）
scripts/pipeline/check-all.sh
scripts/pipeline/check-all.sh dsh-auto-upgrade dsh-plugin-product-subagents   # 只跑指定插件

# 在一次性 $DSH_HOME 里验证插件能被 profile 正确安装 + 组合（绝不触碰真实 ~/.dsh）
scripts/pipeline/install-check.sh
scripts/pipeline/install-check.sh dsh-plugin-product-subagents
```

- **本仓库的「交付物」不是线上服务，而是「插件被本机 DSH profile 正确装配」**——对应 `install-check.sh`，
  它每个插件新建一个 `mktemp -d` 的 `DSH_HOME`，`pnpm dlx @deepseek-ai/dsh@<当前版本> plugin --profile headless add <插件>`
  后用 `--dump-config` 校验，装完即删。
- ⚠️ **`dsh-im-bridge-workspaces` 无法独立 `pnpm install`**（干净 checkout 里必然失败，原因见
  [issue #3](https://github.com/guraul/self-dsh-plugins/issues/3)：其 `peerDependencies` 用 `*` 会解析到陈旧的
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session@0.0.1-rc.1`，后者依赖未发布的内部包 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-type-meta`）。
  所以它**不进 `check-all.sh` 的常规测试路径**，CI 里也**只做 `node --check` 语法门禁**并打印跳过原因；
  完整校验走 `scripts/pipeline/install-check.sh dsh-im-bridge-workspaces`（一次性 DSH profile 里装配）。
- 只读状态一览：`scripts/pipeline/status.sh`。
- CI（`.github/workflows/ci.yml`）只跑测试 + `node --check`，**零部署步骤**；`dsh-im-bridge-workspaces`
  那一项 `install: false`，即跳过安装 / 测试 / typecheck，只跑语法门禁。

## 开发流程

每个任务走 issue → worktree → PR → review → squash 合并（**没有部署**）：

```sh
scripts/pipeline/new-task.sh <issue号>

plugins.description: dsh-cn-doc-formatter · DSH 插件
plugins.readme_text:
# @deepwhale-cn/dsh-cn-doc-formatter

[![Listed on DSH Plugin Hub](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/zh/plugins/feely0208/dsh-cn-doc-formatter)


## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @deepwhale-cn/dsh-cn-doc-formatter
```
**中文公文排版** —— 给 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 用的 skill 插件。

按 **GB/T 9704-2012《党政机关公文格式》** 生成 `.docx` / `.pdf` / `.txt`，
并自带**输出自检**——生成完逐项核对页边距、字号、行距、字体、页面尺寸，
不符合规范就报错，而不是让你交付一份看起来差不多、实际不合规的文件。

## ⚠️ 本插件不含字体，字体需你自备

**这是刻意的设计，不是缺失。**

公文规范要求的仿宋（方正仿宋等）是**商业字体**。其授权允许你在文档中使用，
但**不允许再分发字体文件本身**。所以本插件只做「排版引擎」，字体由你提供：

```bash
# 方式一：直接指定字体文件（推荐，最明确）
export DSH_CN_FANGSONG=/path/to/仿宋.ttf
export DSH_CN_FANGSONG_BOLD=/path/to/仿宋加粗.ttf   # 可选

# 方式二：指定一个目录，脚本在其中按文件名查找
export DSH_CN_FONT_DIR=~/my-fonts
```

也可以直接装进**系统字体目录**（一次装好处处可用）：

| 系统 | 目录 |
|---|---|
| macOS | `~/Library/Fonts/` |
| Windows | `C:\Windows\Fonts\` |
| Linux | `~/.fonts/` 或 `~/.local/share/fonts/` |

装 WPS Office 也行 —— 它自带方正仿宋。

**找不到字体时不会静默失败**：PDF 退回系统宋体，并在 stderr 打印上面这张获取指引。
docx 只在文件里声明字体族名（由你机器上的 Word 渲染），不依赖字体文件。

> **一个细节**：如果你只有常规仿宋、没有加粗体，**标题会继续使用仿宋**（只是不加粗），
> 而不是换成宋体。因为「全文统一仿宋」是硬规范，宁可字重不够也不换字体族。
> reportlab 不做合成粗体，这是引擎限制。

## 它管什么

| 项目 | 规范值 |
|---|---|
| 标题 | 仿宋，二号（22pt）加粗，居中，行距 33–36 磅 |
| 一/二/三/四级标题 | 仿宋，三号（16pt）加粗，左空二字 |
| 正文 | 仿宋，四号（14pt），固定行距 28 磅，首行缩进严格 2 字 |
| 版头（可选） | 份号 / 密级 / 紧急程度 / 发文字号，仿宋三号 |
| 署名与日期 | 距正文下空 3 行，日期阿拉伯数字右空 4 字 |
| 页码 | 「- 1 -」，单页居右空一字、双页居左空一字 |
| 页边距 | 上 3.7 / 下 3.5 / 左 2.8 / 右 2.6 cm |
| 文档网格 | 每面 22 行、每行 28 字 |

**不出现任何 AI 痕迹**：无水印、无生成标记、无作者信息、无版本说明、无注释。

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @deepwhale-cn/dsh-cn-doc-formatter
```

然后重启 dsh。技能会在 agent 需要时自动可用。

### Python 依赖

排版脚本是 Python，需要这些库：

```bash
pip install python-docx reportlab fontTools pypdf
```

| 库 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| `python-docx` | 生成 Word 文档 |
| `reportlab` | 生成 PDF |
| `fontTools` | 探测本机已装字体（读字体 name 表） |
| `pypdf` | 自检时校验 PDF 是否真的嵌入了目标字体 |

## 它比「套个模板」多做了什么

**1. 输出自检（`verify_output.py`）**

生成完不是结束。自检会真的打开产出文件，逐项核对：

```
  ── 公文.docx
     ✅ 上边距 3.70cm ✓      ✅ 标题 22pt 加粗 ✓
     ✅ 正文 14.0pt / 行距 28pt ✓
     ✅ 全文统一字体：FangS-SC ✓
  ── 公文.pdf
     ✅ 嵌入字体：/AAAAAA+FangS-SC, /AAAAAA+FangS-SC-Bold
     ✅ 页面 A4 21.0×29.7cm ✓
```

退出码 `0` = 通过，`1` = 有不符合项 —— **可以直接用在 CI 或交付卡口上**。

**2. Markdown 输入适配（`md_adapter.py`）**

内容常以 Markdown 写就，直接喂给脚本会丢失层级（整篇被当正文）：

| Markdown | 转成 | 公文层级 |
|---|---|---|
| `## 一、小节` | `一、小节` | 一级标题 |
| `### 1.1 小节` | `（一）小节` | 二级标题 |
| `#### 更深` | `1. 小节` | 三级标题 |
| `- 列表项` | 正文 | 正文 |
| `\| 表格 \|` | `表头：值；表头：值。` | 正文 |

它还会把同一段内的软换行合并成一行 —— 源文档常手动折行，
逐行当独立段落会在断句处留下孤立标点（如单独一行的「、」）。

**3. 跨平台字体探测**

早期实现用 `fc-list` 探测字体，而 **macOS 不预装 fontconfig**，
异常被吞掉后恒返回「字体不存在」，于是**即使装了仿宋也检测不到**，会始终走回退分支。
本版改为直接读字体文件的 `name` 表，macOS / Windows / Linux 通用。

## 用法

技能正文里有完整命令。核心三条：

```bash
# 生成 Word / PDF
python "<插件目录>/scripts/docx_formatter.py" --output <目录> \
  --title "标题" --body "正文..." --sender "发文机关" --date "2026年9月25日"
python "<插件目录>/scripts/pdf_formatter.py"  --output <目录> \
  --title "标题" --body "正文..." --sender "发文机关" --date "2026年9月25日"

# 输出自检（不要跳过）
python "<插件目录>/scripts/verify_output.py" --dir <输出目录>
```

> ⚠️ **早期文档里的 `--type notice` 参数并不存在**，加上会直接报
> `unrecognized arguments`。文种由内容决定，脚本不做区分。本版已修正文档。

## 设计取舍

**不分发字体。** 见上文——这不是省事，是避免把商业字体的再分发风险
转嫁给每一个使用者。

**不联网。** 排版、字体探测、自检全部在本地完成，不把文档内容发往任何第三方服务。

**文种不参与排版。** 通知 / 报告 / 函 / 决定的排版规范是一致的，
差别只在正文怎么写。脚本不为文种分叉，避免维护一堆看似不同实则相同的模板。

## 与其它插件的关系

按 [DSH 插件生态倡议书](https://github.com/anywhere-labs/dsh-desktop/blob/main/docs/plugin-ecosystem.md)
的三条原则开发：**组合优先、声明清晰、兼容优先**。不假设、不覆盖其它插件的内部实现。

## 许可

MIT。**本软件不包含任何字体文件**；使用者在文档中选用何种字体，由使用者自行负责
取得该字体的合法授权。

plugins.description: 面向 DeepSeek Harness 的 Claude Code 风格终端界面，支持 Windows、macOS 与 Linux，兼容透明终端、VS Code 主题和自定义配色。
plugins.readme_text:
> **Release compatibility:** The current tested Host is official `0.2.0-rc.2`. SeekTTY `1.3.0` is paired with that Host. See the [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md) for changes and installation, and the [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md) for exact package evidence.

SeekTTY

A terminal workspace for DeepSeek Harness.

Overview · Quick start · Clarify and Plan · Features · Compatibility

English · 中文

--- ## Overview Run `deepseek` from a project directory to use the native Agent, Session, model, permission, Settings, Profile, plugin, and persistence services of [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) in one terminal workspace. SeekTTY is the terminal surface; Harness remains the owner of runtime state. Models, Providers, Agent Presets, permissions, commands, tools, Settings, Skills, MCP servers, and marketplace sources are discovered from the running Harness. Capabilities added by upstream or third-party Bundles therefore appear without being hard-coded into SeekTTY. For requirements that still need definition, the optional [Clarify Host plugin](https://github.com/Hilbert-beinghappy/dsh-plugin-clarify) adds a guided `/clarify` workflow. It asks focused questions, updates a reviewable Draft after each answer, and returns the accepted Draft to the composer. Harness-native `/plan` can then turn the submitted requirement into an implementation plan. ## Development checkout Build and install a local SeekTTY package from the repository root: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm run build pnpm pack dsh plugin --profile tui add --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false ./seektty-1.3.0.tgz dsh --profile tui ``` Use the local tarball for source development and testing. For the released package, use the exact npm version below. ## Quick start Install the published SeekTTY release on its verified official DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2`: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 dsh plugin --profile tui add --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false seektty@1.3.0 dsh --profile tui ``` These commands install the prebuilt Bundle through native `dsh plugin` reconciliation. The per-command pnpm option avoids the pnpm 11 Global Virtual Store layout that the Cordis loader in the currently tested dsh releases cannot reliably load. SeekTTY never changes global pnpm configuration. Clarify and Auxiliary Runtime are optional, not default dependencies; their historical joint acceptance is listed under [Compatibility](#compatibility-and-verification). The exact `seektty@1.3.0` npm package is documented in the [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md), [PR audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md), and [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md). ### Bare `deepseek` launcher After installing `dsh`, install the same SeekTTY release globally and pin Profile reconciliation to its exact npm version: ```sh pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false seektty@1.3.0 export SEEKTTY_SPEC=seektty@1.3.0 deepseek ``` PowerShell uses the same exact npm spec: ```powershell pnpm add --global --config.enable-global-virtual-store=false 'seektty@1.3.0' $env:SEEKTTY_SPEC='seektty@1.3.0' deepseek ``` `deepseek` requires `dsh` on `PATH`, or `DSH_BIN` pointing to its executable. Common launch forms include: ```sh deepseek "check this project" deepseek --cwd ../project deepseek --resume deepseek --resume deepseek --profile team-tui deepseek --version deepseek --update ``` `deepseek --update` is self-first: it checks SeekTTY before dsh, installs at most one compatible component per run, and never installs an untested gap or future Host. `DSH_BIN`, local installs, and `SEEKTTY_SPEC` overrides are left unchanged. Update failures do not block startup. Set `SEEKTTY_UPDATE=check` for a post-session notice or `SEEKTTY_UPDATE=0` to disable checks. SeekTTY `1.3.0` supports official dsh `0.2.0-rc.2` and brings more native workflows into the terminal. See the bilingual [release notes](docs/release-v1.3.0.md), [complete PR audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md), and [verification record](docs/release-v1.3.0-verification.md). ### What's new in 1.3.0 - Access native Session actions, plans and artifacts, MCP resources, Team information, schedules, timed/continued questions, and account/model information from the terminal. - Browse Host workspace files with text/binary views and available file watching. Plugins can add terminal Session actions and guarded draft input activities with undo. - Install optional Creator, Browser, or Computer companion Bundles when you need them. With the official voice-input Bundle enabled, `/speech wav` provides reviewed WAV transcription; it does not record from the microphone. - Fix current-Host preset/forms/tool-result handling, stale targets, approval display, watcher cleanup, and bounded shutdown. Keep native Harness ownership and the existing terminal workflows. The release notes also fill gaps in the `1.2.6` summary: Agent Tree navigation, semantic transcript copying, target-specific context menus, Provider configuration, VS Code theme discovery, independent appearance controls, native scrollback, and long-session rendering fixes. Those features were already shipped; the [audit](docs/release-v1.3.0-pr-audit.md) identifies their original PRs and versions. ## Interface | DeepSeek light | DeepSeek dark | | --- | --- | | ![SeekTTY DeepSeek light start screen](assets/seektty-tui.png) | ![SeekTTY DeepSeek dark start screen](assets/seektty-tui-dark.png) | | TypeScript in the light interface | Tools, file reads, and Diff in the dark interface | | --- | --- | | ![SeekTTY light TypeScript syntax highlighting](assets/seektty-code-light.png) | ![SeekTTY dark tool and Diff syntax highlighting](assets/seektty-code-dark.png) | Full mode uses a fixed alternate-screen viewport and keeps the composer and status at the bottom. Its mouse support browses history, selects text, and clicks existing controls inside SeekTTY. F3 or `/mouse native` switches while idle to terminal-native mode: SeekTTY leaves the alternate screen, writes the complete loaded conversation to ordinary terminal scrollback, disables mouse reporting, and lets the terminal or tmux own scrolling, search, and selection. Backfill is sequential and reports progress; Esc stops it without stopping the Session, while Ctrl+L refreshes only the active tail. `/transcript` opens transcript browsing and `/transcript replay` explicitly writes the available conversation again. Images use a textual attachment row in native mode. Already-written history is not recolored or reflowed by SeekTTY; the terminal owns that history. An empty session now opens with a responsive Fastfetch-style welcome page rather than sendable task suggestions. The default uses a packaged, original-color DeepSeek pixel whale plus runtime facts from the current Profile; it does **not** execute Fastfetch. The first-time API-key prompt remains higher priority and finishes before option

plugins.description: Session cost and billing metrics for the DSH Web GUI: what this conversation cost, what the cache saved, and whether the current hour is peak or off-peak. A companion to the shipped stats pills, never a duplicate of them.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-session-metrics

Session **cost and billing** metrics for the DSH Web GUI — what this conversation cost, what the
cache saved, and whether the current hour is peak or off-peak. Built as a companion to the shipped
stats pills, never a duplicate of them.

## Why

The shipped stats pills report tokens and context, and stop short of money. That leaves three
questions unanswered, and the obvious answer to each is a lie:

**A model with no rate card is not free.** An unpriceable provider reads `unpriced` and shows its
tokens; a genuinely free model ships a card of zeros and reads a real `$0.00`. The two must not
render alike — `unpriced` means *no card*, and an unpriced pair is never rendered as a number.

**A newly integrated provider arrives silently.** DSH reports usage per provider and model; rates are
configuration. Integrate a provider before its rates are entered — the case that happened with
OpenRouter — and every figure for it is missing with nothing on the page saying why. The session
detail names the pair it observed with no card, and the tokens it used.

**Peak pricing is invisible until it is a surprise.** DeepSeek bills peak and off-peak at different
rates, in the provider's own timezone. Whether *right now* is peak is not something a user should
have to derive.

## Agent Skills

Installing the plugin registers the **`session-metrics`** skill, so an agent can explain the figures
and reconfigure the rates without reading the source. Ask it what a session cost, whether a model is
priced, or how to add a rate card for a provider it has seen.

## Quick Start

The plugin installs into your DSH **profile** by link — it is not published to npm, so the clone is
the source. Both routes end with a **restart**.

### Option A — the script

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mrdhira/dsh-session-metrics.git ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics
cd ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics
./install.sh                 # builds, registers in your profile, runs pnpm install
```

It accepts `--profile <dir>` to target a profile other than `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop`, `--check` to
report what would change without writing anything, and `--remove` to unregister.

### Option B — the manual steps

**1. Clone it somewhere stable** (this path becomes your install path):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mrdhira/dsh-session-metrics.git ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics
cd ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics
```

**2. Build it.** `pnpm install` runs the `prepare` script, which builds `lib/**` — the part DSH
actually loads. It is generated; never hand-edit it.

```bash
pnpm install
```

**3. Register it with your profile** — the dependency and the bundle name, with an absolute path:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "dsh-session-metrics": "link:/Users/<you>/.dsh/plugins/dsh-session-metrics"
  },
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": [
        "dsh-session-metrics"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**4. Install the link, then restart DSH:**

```bash
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop && pnpm install
```

Nothing needs adding to `cordis.patch.yml`: the bundle declares its own Loader row.

> **Restart, don't reload.** The host half loads once per app process, so a host-side change needs a
> full quit and reopen (`⌘Q`, then reopen). A page reload does not pick it up. A client-side (UI)
> change needs the bundle toggled in the plugin manager.

### Verify it is really working

A strip should appear below the composer with `cost`, `saved` and a peak indicator. If it does not:

- `lib/v1/index.js` exists — if not, `pnpm install` did not finish building;
- the profile's `package.json` names `dsh-session-metrics` in **both** `dependencies` and
  `dsh.profile.bundles`;
- DSH was **restarted** after installing.

An `unpriced` chip means a working install with no matching rate card — not a failure. See
[Configure](#configure).

### Configure

**A fresh install needs no configuration.** Rate cards ship for `deepseek-account`,
`deepseek-official`, `netra-runtime` and `openrouter`, so the cost chip works immediately. OpenRouter
ships **only the models its own catalog marks free** (the `:free` suffix and the free-models router)
at zero rates; its paid models deliberately carry no card, because DSH reports no prices for them and
a fabricated rate is worse than a named gap.

Rates are edited in the GUI: **Plugins sidebar → `dsh-session-metrics`**. The same table can be set
in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: session-metrics
  name: dsh-session-metrics
  config:
    display: { currency: USD, primaryProvider: deepseek-account }
    budget: { sessionUsd: 5, warnAt: 0.75 }
    providers:
      - id: my-router
        models:
          - model: some/model
            rates: { flat: { cacheHit: 0.01, cacheMiss: 0.1, output: 0.25 } }
        billing: { windows: [] }      # no peak concept
```

Rates are USD per 1M tokens. A model takes **either** a `flat` row **or** a `peak` row with
`offPeak`. A provider with no `billing.windows` is flat and shows no peak chip.

> **A `providers:` list in your patch replaces the shipped cards** rather than adding to them. Pin your
> own providers and the OpenRouter free cards stop shipping with them — add a card for each pair you
> need, or let **Seen, unpriced** name the ones you missed.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `display.currency` | `USD` | `USD` or `CNY` |
| `display.primaryProvider` | — | hides the provider chip when the session uses this provider |
| `display.chips` | all | which chips to show, and in what order: `peak`, `time`, `cost`, `saved`, `provider`, `budget` |
| `budget.sessionUsd` | off | per-session ceiling; omit to disable |
| `budget.warnAt` | `0.75` | fraction of the budget at which the strip warns |

The full rate-card format, the shipped cards and the reasoning behind them are in
[`docs/pricing.md`](docs/pricing.md).

## How it Works

Costs are derived from the Host's own `tokenUsage` projection — the same source the stats pills read
— so this plugin adds interpretation, not a second ledger. Cache savings compare each cache-hit token
against the rate that would have been paid on a miss, per the card in effect. Peak and off-peak
windows resolve in the provider's own timezone, holidays included, and the countdown is computed once
a minute while the detail view is open rather than on every render.

Two surfaces, one projection:

- **the strip**, below the composer: cost, cache savings, the peak state with your local time, the
  provider when it is not your configured primary, and budget progress;
- **the detail**, on click: the cost breakdown (cache-hit / miss / write / output), cache savings and
  blended rate, the rate window with a countdown, cost per step, cost per model when a session
  switched models, and the projections each figure came from.

The plugin deliberately does **not** render session token totals, cache-hit rate, context percentage,
turns, steps or tok/s — the shipped pills own those. [`docs/data-sources.md`](docs/data-sources.md)
records which projection feeds which figure, which is what keeps the two from drifting back into
duplication.

### Requirements

- **DSH** with the Web GUI, and a profile you can edit (`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/`).
- **Node.js 22+** and **pnpm** to build from source. The built artifact needs nothing extra at
  runtime.

### Development

```bash
pnpm install                  # deps + build (prepare)
pnpm run build                # rebuild lib/**
pnpm test                     # 111 tests: 105 pass, 6 skipped without a session log
pnpm run typecheck            # three projects: host, browser half, tests
pnpm run test:fast            # host logic only — the quick loop
pnpm run test:dom             # the UI half under jsdom
DSH_SESSION_LOG=<path>.jsonl.zstd pnpm run test:replay   # replays a real session
```

```
src/host/*.ts         host half: config schema, projection, ledger, pricing  -> lib/v1/index.js
src/client/index.cts  browser half: strip, detail panel, pricing page        -> lib/v1/client.js
types/dsh.d.ts        the DSH surfaces this plugin uses (the app ships no .d.ts)
build.mjs             esbuild: ESM host half, CJS browser half + loader h

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex — native subagent progress, in-host worker sessions with per-tier presets, and a multimodal bridge that lends the text-only harness vision and image generation.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Crew

A DeepSeek Harness plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok, without giving up the host's native subagent UI.
Native Progress UI • Tier Policy & Escalation • Dispatch Guardrails • Jobs Board • In-Host DSH Sessions • Vision & Image Gen (Native-First) • One-Click Install

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-crew · Current plugin release: 0.1.0-rc.11 · Tested with DSH 0.1.1-rc.1

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The DSH Crew settings page — host integrations, dispatch policy, execution and the multimodal bridge

## Why DSH Crew DSH Crew is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) — an open-source agent harness. It makes DSH agents dispatchable from Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok: the orchestrator keeps its own model, the work runs on a real DSH agent with that harness's tools, sandbox, presets and session history, and the host still shows it as a native subagent with live progress. What runs the work is a DSH agent, not a bare model call. Tiers (`flash` / `pro`) select how much capability that agent gets from the harness's configured roster — DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro today — so a change of model in DSH needs no change here.
### 🧵 Native Progress UI Workers appear as regular subagents in Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok — dispatch count, running step, tool calls and token usage all show up in the host's own task panel, plus a claude-hud statusline segment: `⚙dsh 1▶pro 2m14s 21.7k/606 ✓3`. ### 🎚️ Tier Policy and Escalation `flash` for mechanical work, `pro` for reasoning, `effort` from `off` to `max`. `tier_policy` can clamp every dispatch to one tier at the tool layer, and `escalate_on_failure` retries a failed flash run once on pro — based on evidence, not on guessing difficulty up front.
### 🏛️ In-Host DSH Sessions With the bundle installed in a DSH profile, each worker is a first-class DSH session: visible in the Web UI, grouped by working directory, mounted with the Agent preset you choose per tier. Without DSH running, dispatch falls back to a standalone DSH runtime, so CI and headless environments still work. ### 👁️ Vision and Image Generation DSH's models are text-only. `describe_image` now prefers DeepSeek's own VL model (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) whenever a key is available, then falls back to the CLIs you already have — Claude, Codex, Grok, Antigravity — or any OpenAI-compatible API you configure. `generate_image` borrows the same CLIs' brush. Pasted images stay visible in the conversation and reach the model as text.
### 🛡️ Dispatch Guardrails Every dispatch is checked before anything spawns. Worker→worker nesting is capped at origin-chain depth 3 and cycles are refused; a second worker on a workspace another job already holds is refused with the holder's info — never silently queued. Refusals are readable errors: wait or re-scope, don't bypass. ### 📋 Jobs Board The DSH Crew panel doubles as a jobs board: every worker job — running or finished — is listed with tier, effort, live progress and tokens, held workspaces show their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (e.g. a hub restart) is surfaced as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.
### 🔌 Custom Providers Bring your own endpoint (Base URL + API key + models) or a local command template. Each provider has a connectivity test that checks reachability and auth, then makes one real vision call so you find out now, not mid-task. ### 📦 One-Click Install The settings page installs and updates the Claude Code plugin, the Codex role files and the Antigravity / Grok agents, skills and commands for you — marketplace registration, permission allowlist, HUD wiring, absolute paths rendered for this machine — and restores them just as easily. Every settings file is backed up first.
## How it works ``` Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok (orchestrator, keeps its own model) └─ ds-flash / ds-pro ← native subagent shell (progress shows in the host's task UI) └─ MCP: dsh_run_worker(tier, effort, cwd, worker=) ├─ worker="agy"/"grok" → that external CLI runs the task (explicit opt-in) ├─ hub reachable → session inside DSH (visible in the Web UI, grouped by cwd) └─ otherwise → dsh-jsonrpc-agent runtime (worker.cordis.yml) └─ DeepSeek V4 Flash / Pro (DSH SDK, event stream → progress and token stats) ``` ## One run, two views Dispatch fans out. Below, eighteen workers translate this README in parallel: the host counts them as its own subagents, while the harness runs them as real sessions.

Claude Code sees dsh-crew workers as native subagents, with a statusline segment tracking running tiers, elapsed time and tokens.

The DSH Crew panel sees the same run from the harness side: which host dispatched each job, its tier and effort, live progress and token usage.

The panel is also the jobs board: running and finished jobs stay listed with tier, progress and tokens, held workspaces name their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (a hub restart) surfaces as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.

## Install Install into a DSH profile from npm: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-crew@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-crew dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately. ### Configure DeepSeek credentials (standalone only) In hub mode — the installation above — workers run inside the DSH instance and use the DeepSeek credentials it is already configured with. Nothing else to set up. Only the standalone fallback needs a key of its own: dispatching from a host with no DSH instance running launches a worker runtime as a separate process.
